Battlefield is visually stunning and has great potential, but the gameplay experience is currently broken due to extreme latency dependency.
The Problem: Netcode & High Ping
The game relies entirely on your connection. Even a 1ms difference in ping creates a massive disadvantage that is clearly noticeable during gunfights. My experience has been terrible because:
• TTK (Time to Kill) is inconsistent: I often find myself shooting first and landing an entire magazine into an enemy's chest, only for them to turn around and kill me instantly.
• Desync: On my screen, I am hitting them, but due to the ping, the server doesn't register the damage.
Server Status
Since the Middle East servers were closed, I am forced to play with a ping of 80ms. While this might seem "average" in some games, in Battlefield, it makes the game practically unplayable and unfair.
Final Verdict
I cannot recommend Battlefield in its current state. If you don't live right next to a server, you will struggle. It’s incredibly frustrating to lose matches simply because of network infrastructure rather than skill.
Avoid this game until they address the server issues for our region.

**BF6 = AMAZING GAME RUINED BY FORCED CROSSPLAY**

Battlefield veteran since Battlefield 1942, and honestly… this game COULD have been the perfect Battlefield.

BUT they completely ruined it for PC players with one thing:
FORCED CROSSPLAY.

PC players CANNOT disable crossplay. No option. Nothing. So you are permanently forced to play against console players abusing ridiculously overpowered aim assist that feels straight-up like legal aimbot.

If PC players had the option to turn crossplay OFF, this game would honestly be incredible.

Instead, every fight feels fake:

* console players tracking perfectly through smoke and recoil (which is heavily reduced on console)
* instant lock-on at close range
* zero human error thanks to aim assist doing half the work

And on top of that:

* terrible netcode
* random hit registration
* constant desync
* dying meters behind cover

How do you make gunplay-focused FPS games for 20+ years and STILL have netcode this bad?

Maps are mid overall, except Siege of Cairo which is actually fun.

What frustrates me the most is that the core game is GOOD. The atmosphere, destruction, sounds, movement… it’s all there. But forced crossplay completely destroys the experience for PC players.

This could have been the perfect Battlefield. Instead, it’s another frustrating mess.

I normally do not write reviews at all, but had to for what i've seen,

Battlefield 6 had a rough start. At launch, it felt incomplete—maps were too small, the focus seemed to be on microtransactions, more specifically a free-to-play battle royale mode rather than delivering the core Battlefield experience. For a lot of modern releases, that kind of launch can feel like the game is destined to be abandoned.

However, 8 months in, the developers have shown a real commitment to listening and improving. The game has grown in ways that actually matter: bigger maps, meaningful updates, and a clear focus on fixing the gameplay rather than chasing trends. It feels like the devs are truly redeeming the game and building toward what it should have been at launch.

What I really appreciate is that, even with the microtransactions, they’ve kept things grounded. Everything added fits the military theme—no cartoonish cosmetics, no anime guns, no magic bullets, no celebrity skins—just the authentic Battlefield vibe.

If this trajectory continues, I genuinely believe that one year post-launch, BF6 will feel like a completely different, fully realized game. It’s exciting to see a franchise I love being treated with this level of care and attention, and I’m optimistic about the future.

8/10 now, with the potential to climb higher as the updates continue. This is a game worth revisiting and keeping an eye on.

Easily one of the best shooters available currently, and a pretty great battlefield. I have had 250 hours so far and will have a lot more during the lifespan of the game. A lot of the criticism doesn't ring true to me, or is exaggerated in my opinion. There is some fair criticism that I agree with:

-The maps are a bit small, but not as bad as some people make out, this is still far from COD and the new maps are much bigger. It does play faster than the older games though so be aware. 
-The old premium model was better than the new battlepass model, and progression for a casual player is a bit slow. 
-The gun balance is a bit strange with SMGs still being pretty good at range whilst some assault rifles struggle. I always use a mix of guns though so it doesn't bother me much. 
-The biggest actual complaint that affects my actual experience was half-empty lobbies being back-filled by bots instead of players. This was a real problem for a long while (6 months ish) but seems to be fixed now (fingers crossed).

  Mostly though I've had a great time. Not watching or engaging with social media has no doubt helped as there is lots of content out there designed to make people annoyed. I played BF1942, BFBC2, BF3 a lot, BF1 a lot, BF5, some BF2042, and now this. This is a mostly great game, and still provides an experience unique to Battlefield. 

  The visuals are fantastic, the audio is amazing, the gunplay is great, sniping feels excellent, the performance has been excellent for me (maxed settings on a high end rig). If you really enjoy battlefield then I would just buy this and enjoy it, and ignore most of the noise surrounding it. You don't need BF Pro so don't worry about buying the battlepass unless you really want to.

ah Battlefield, was ist nur aus dir geworden? Ich fange erstmal mit dem Positivem an und will nicht direkt ins Negativ. Keine Frage, die Open beta hat mit Freunden im Squad echt spaß gemacht, sodass man das Desaster nach Bf 2024 schnell wieder vergessen hat. Die Intensiven Kämpfe, heftige Explosionen und die Häuserkämpfe waren sehr stressig aber es hat Spaß gemacht. 

Nun nach mittlerweiler Zwei Season's sehe ich und paar meiner Freunde wohin dieses Battlefield hin geht. Die Matches spielen sich alle gleich. Gegner benutzen immer die selben cod-ählichen Waffen (meist MP;SMG oder Sturmgewehre, sodass nur auf KD gegangen wird. Klassenrollen werden nur selten von einigen richtig gespielt. Spawnsystem ist für die Mülltonne, wie oft bin ich einfach neben Gegner im eigenen Bereich gespawnt?! Es ist mehr ein run & gun als strategisches Vorgehen, was in alten Teilen viel besser funktoniert hat. Die Maps sind viel zu klein und alles wirkt blass und eintönig. Matchmaking kann man komplett vergessen, meist gewinnt oder verliert man eine Runde mit knapp 500-800 Tickets Vorsprung + manche Maps sind total unbalanced, je nach dem auf welcher Seite man startet. 

Die Leute die mit Black Ops 7 unzufrieden sind, werden wohl hier ihren Spaß haben. Ich bin hiermit raus. Wir sehen uns auf den alten Schlachtfeldern in Battlefield 1&5 wieder! Dort machen die Kämpfe nach knapp 10 Jahren immernoch spaß und optisch sehen die beiden Teile noch dazu viel besser aus. Außerdem hat man mit den behemoths aus dem ersten Teil ein cooles feature eingebaut, sodass das benachteiligte Team immernoch ein Chance hat das Match zu wenden. In Battlefield 6 spielt sich jeder Modus identisch und es gibt nichts an das man sich noch später erinnert. Gunplay, Sound, Chaos stimmen für das moderne Setting – aber es fehlt die Battlefield‑Identität, die früher ganze Abende legendär gemacht hat. So ist es leider wie jeder andere Shooter. Teamplay, taktische Tiefe & große Schlachten wird man hier leider nicht finden.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I’ll start with the positive things first. The open beta was really fun, especially when playing in a squad with friends. It made me forget the disaster of BF 2042 for a moment. The intense fights, the heavy explosions, and the close‑quarters combat were stressful, but in a good way.

But now, after two seasons, my friends and I can clearly see where this Battlefield is heading. All matches feel the same. Enemies always use the same CoD‑like weapons (mostly SMGs or assault rifles), and everyone only plays for their KD. Class roles are rarely used the way they should be. The spawn system is terrible — I spawned next to enemies in our own area so many times. It’s more run & gun than strategic gameplay, which worked much better in the older games. The maps are too small and everything looks bland and repetitive. Matchmaking is also useless; you usually win or lose with a 500–800 ticket difference. Some maps are completely unbalanced depending on which side you start on.

People who are unhappy with Black Ops 7 will probably enjoy this game. But I’m done. I’ll return to the old battlefields in Battlefield 1 and 5. Those games are still fun even after almost 10 years, and they still look better. BF1’s behemoths were a great feature that gave the losing team a real chance to turn the match around. In Battlefield 6, every mode feels the same and there’s nothing memorable about it. The gunplay, sound, and chaos are good for a modern setting — but the Battlefield identity is missing. The identity that once made whole evenings unforgettable. Now it feels like every other shooter. You won’t find teamplay, tactical depth, or large‑scale battles here anymore.
So much potential yet they manage to F.up this. Just Unbelievable

Where to begin with this game.
First, a disclaimer. I play mainly Conquest, and sometimes branch out into other gamemodes. But I would wager 95% of my playtime is in Conquest, and as such my opinions are based almost exclusively on that one gamemode (and a little bit of rush)

Being a Battlefield veteran, playing Battlefield 2 on the family PC as a child, but having most of my playtime in BF3 and 4, this game is in no way a perfect Battlefield game, but it is absolutely a step in the right direction after the last couple of entries to the series.

Season 3, with the release of Golmud, makes the game feel more like BF3 and BF4 than any other entry since those two. But, because of course there's a but, this one map that has the feeling and gameplay of a proper Battlefield map does not make up for the many shortcomings of the game.

Recoil still feels soulless on all weapons, with only minor differences between every weapons handling.
Basically every map feels pretty much the same, with the typical 3 lane layout, with limited proper flanking routes. The verticality of many of the maps is also quite lacking, and the maps with verticality are often not by design, but just people getting on top of massive rocks or mountains in the middle or edges of the maps, and sitting there for the entire game. Those rocks are also a part of the design problem, with the 3 lane design I mentioned earlier. The rocks or mountains make up the split between the lanes, and feel like exactly that: a design choice to divide the map right down the middle, which feels soulless and artificial.
Besides the 3 lane layouts of many of the maps, there is also just a major lack in variety of the maps. All of the maps can be put into 3 major categories (and one minor category that only Golmud fits into).
The first of these categories i call "Close quarters spamageddon" reminiscent of Operation Metro but without the actually fun map layout, the second is "Somewhat big empty death trap", and the final major category I call "Generic city centre map".
The fourth category, exlusively fitting Golmud for now, is "Somewhat varied and balanced large map", and this category is in my opinion what the map designers should strive for with most of the maps.
Golmud is, at this very moment, the absolutely best map in the game in my opinion. Vehicles are in abundance, and can be easily countered if you have competent teammates (and half a brain yourself). The map has large empty areas, but there are lanes between the points and through the empty areas, with a variety of cover for infantry. The map is in no way perfect, but it is the only actually [i] fun [/i] map in the game at this moment for me. I am however biased towards vehicle gameplay, both ground and air, so take this opinion with a grain of salt if you yourself prefer infantry gameplay.

The gameplay itself, however, is quite fun. The gunplay isn't perfect, but it's much more engaging and fun than BF2042. The movement is fast, but not too fast, and feels smooth. And thank god the operator system is gone.
The performance of the game is alright. My setup runs most maps at almost ultra settings, 1440p, at around 80-120 fps, but some of the larger maps, especially Golmud, can dip to about 60 fps later on in the round.

With all of that said would i recommend the game? At full price: hell no. Stay away from the 70€ price tag. I bought it for 42€ I believe, and at that price I'm closer to recommending the game. In it's current state however, the price point I believe the game is worth is roughly €30, and no higher. The biggest reasoning for this is the lack of interesting maps.

Also two things to be aware of:
The amount of whining in the in-game chat is unbearable. I recommend turning it off completely.
Crossplay can't be turned off on PC. Not that I personally have a problem with playing against people using controllers. I do however have a problem with the fact there simply is no in-game option to turn crossplay off for PC players.

I've been having a blast with Battlefield 6. The game is simply fun. Pure, addictive fun. Every time I launch it I end up playing way longer than I planned because the gameplay loop just clicks.

What I appreciate most is how active the developers are. You can clearly see they're listening to the community and constantly patching the things that actually annoy players. The game feels cared for and it's getting better with every update. That's rare these days and it makes me want to keep coming back.

The gameplay itself is exactly what I want from Battlefield: dynamic, fast paced, and chaotic in the best possible way. Big maps, proper vehicle play, intense infantry fights, and those "only in Battlefield" moments that still happen regularly. It feels like the series has finally remembered what made it special.

The endless comparisons to BF4 are honestly getting a bit tiring. 
It's the same thing people did with every new Heroes of Might and Magic after Heroes 3 - treating the old game like an untouchable legend. Yes, BF4 was amazing, but that doesn't mean this game can't be great in its own way. I'm having more fun here than I had in years with the series.

If you enjoy fast, destructive, large-scale multiplayer shooters, Battlefield 6 is in a really good place right now. Definitely worth jumping in.

Ruined by Season 3 update. Anything that could possibly even scratch the paintwork of a vehicle has been nerfed whilst the vehicles themselves have then been made even more powerful. Expect to see literally everyone having to play engineer as tanks and IFVs slaughter everyone, sponging infinite rocket hits, literally deleting mines at the press of a button (the same mines that no longer have a prayer of killing said vehicles). DICE seem to only care about vehicle users, and want to remove any impediment to their unstoppable killstreaks. Infantry are merely fodder now.

I absolutely loved this game on release, played battlefield for a decade, love it to bits. But this season 3 update is nothing but coddling to vehicles (which I use, I want vehicles to be powerful when used correctly), as DICE themselves have basically made it impossible to misuse vehicles. Not realising that maybe a tank shouldn't be able to drive into a terrible situation and somehow win every time. That maybe an IFV shouldn't be able to detect mines without even having to bother looking for them (yet somehow people think that is more skillfull than those using mines).

Netcode was fine on release, actually the best on any Battlefield. But then people scapegoated it and DICE for some reason listened to them.

Claymores no longer kill. Javelin still dives into the ground constantly. And despite the "diminishing returns" promised with multiple repairers on one vehicle, the increased vehicle health cancels this out.

DICE for years have been incapable of game balance. Rather than buffing the weaker stuff to match the stronger stuff (the best way to do things), they will do this simultaneously with a nerf on what was considered powerful. So all of a sudden something goes from OP to useless. THAT IS NOT BALANCE.

The Season 3 patch has taken a game I loved to play, that got me hanging out with people I hadn't seen in years. And turned it into an appalling unbalanced vehicular moshpit. Where somehow vehicle users get a free pass in playing poorly whilst infantry have to go above and beyond to even have a cats chance in hell of stopping them. The vehicle imbalance now makes BF4s fall update look tame by comparison.

I can only assume those at DICE are vehicle mains who aren't far off adding invincibility to them.

Battlefield titles are usually best at release, before DICE start fiddling with things with their complete incapability of balancing things even remotely correctly.

Playing with my friends is now the only reason why I may consider booting this up again, and even then its a CHORE to play. And whilst there's a tiny chance this update has been a huge mistake, I know DICE well enough to not hold out for a correction. In a matter of hours, one of my genuinely favourite games of all time has become dross on my hard drive.

And I know there's a lot of the community rejoicing at this update for some reason. And when DICE inevitably ruin your fun, I don't want to hear it, I've protested this stuff for years. You can lie in the bed of your making.

Gameplay is fine. Generally enjoyable. Some frustrating things, some good parts. They did put quite a bit of attention to detail, which was nice. This brings me to why I'm writing this review: unless you play no other games, have a monster of a large PC (SSD space I mean) or are okay with organising your PC according to BF6 updates, don't bother. 

For so much attention to detail, they either: have THE WORST FILE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM IN DIGITAL HISTORY or are the most underhanded, profit-seeking studio that wants you to play no other game besides theirs (which, given that its EA....). Why do I say this? The minimum spec is 55GB required to install. The recommended is 80GB. The actual installed size on my system is 126GB. This is, if you are like me and like to occasionally go back to play the campaign. There is a multiplayer-only install as well. So, size discrepancy aside, this means NOTHING when a new season comes along. New maps, guns, etc. - all the nice goodies. One problem though? It needs an ADDITIONAL, give or take, 150GB ON TOP OF THE EXISTING 126GB!!! That is 276GB space dedicated to BF6 every damn new season. Now keep in mind, while not explicitly stated, you do not want to try run this game on an HDD. That means it has to go on your primary drive (SSD) .

For the average user who has a 512GB drive: 40GB is used by system files/OS, leaving you with about 470ish GB. An additional 50 GB is necessary as a virtual workspace for your PC (unless you want it to crash every 15min). That leaves you with 420GB. That means you effectively have 144GB after BF6 is installed and needs to update for all your videos, music, projects, photos, work programs and files. Perhaps doable, right? Except you are forgetting all those background files that optimising programs don't remove (if you are even running one of those), and that the average game size varies between 30GB -70GB. So good luck uninstalling all those other programs/games every new season if you want to keep playing BF6. (Or you could completely uninstall BF6 then redownload it. That does save a lot of space).

Now, don't get me wrong. The game is, from my perspective at least, genuinely enjoyable. But that hassle every 3 months - hence the rant. Why the actual hell do they need 150GB to update game files... It makes no bloody sense...

Battlefield ruhunu geri getiriyoruz diye çıkıp ortaya yine kimliksiz bir karma bırakmışlar. Eskiden Battlefield dediğin şey; kaosun içinde takım oyunu, atmosfer ve “savaş hissi” demekti. Şimdi ise biri kanat takıp uçuyor, diğeri haritanın öbür ucundan kayıyor, ortalık TikTok montajı gibi olmuş. Serinin ağırlığı ve ciddiyeti resmen buhar olmuş durumda.

En kötü tarafı da oyunun artık “Battlefield anı” yaşatmaması. BF3, BF4 dönemlerinde tank sesi bile adrenalini yükseltirdi. Şimdi çatışmalar plastik gibi hissettiriyor. Haritalar büyük ama ruhsuz, silah hissiyatı tat vermiyor, savaş atmosferi yerine cosplay arenası havası var.

Anti-cheat konusu zaten tam trajikomedi. Daha birkaç maçta garip hareketler yapan adamlara denk geliyorsun. İnsan “acaba gerçekten iyi mi oynuyor yoksa sistem yine uyuyor mu” diye düşünmeden edemiyor. Rekabet hissi yerine güvensizlik oluşuyor.

Grafik ve efekt tarafında güzel duran anlar var ama sadece görüntü oyunu kurtarmıyor. Battlefield serisi bir zamanlar sektör standardıydı, şimdi ise eski oyuncuların hafızasında kalan anıların gölgesinde yaşamaya çalışıyor gibi. Nerde o eski BF’ler dedirtiyor gerçekten.

Как говорится, начали за здравие, а закончили за упокой.

Начнем с самого начала:
Бета была просто великолепной, сразу же захотелось купить игру, что я и сделал, даже учитывая негативный опыт предыдущих частей, которые мягко говоря получились не очень.

Почему я ставлю негативный отзыв - все просто:

1. Разработчики забили болта на ребаланс оружия: пулеметы, штурмовые винтовки - это просто мусор, картинки в этой игре, т.к. есть карабины или богоподобные ПИСТОЛЕТЫ ПУЛЕМЕТЫ, которые на дистанции стреляют лучше любой штурмовой винтовки или пулемета, имеют лучшую точность, скорострельность и итоговый урон. Пистолеты пулеметы подавляют лучше любого ручного пулемета.

2. Регистрация урона - это отдельный разговор. В данной серии всегда были проблемы, но не настолько (хотя поначалу в BF3 примерно также было), но блин, там и мощности другие были, сервера другие и т.п. Негоже как-то в 2025-2026 такую говнорегистрацию делать, ей богу. Фиксить это конечно же мы не будем.

3. Авиация. Если ты умеешь пилотировать авиацию, то в этой игре ты царь и бог. Нет, чтобы облегчать пехоте противодействие авиации, разработчики наоборот усложняют жизнь пехоте, ведь BF6 - это игра про 32 на 32 на технике, да?

4. Поведение оружия, а именно скорость полета пули - такое ощущение, что стреляешь пластиковыми пулями из пластикового оружия, т.к. скорость полета пули ничтожна, при правильном мувменте ты можешь почувствовать себя Джоном Уиком или Нео, т.к. уворот от пули в УПОР не составляет каких-либо проблем.

5. ТТК - это тоже интересная песня. С 10-15 метров у оружия уже серьезно падает урон, что сильно влияет на ТТК. Возвращаемся к п. 4 про пластиковые пули и оружие.

6. Карты - это конечно вообще отдельная песня. Все карты, выпущенные в сезонах - это полнейший шлак. Даже голмуд умудрились засрать.

В общем, что я могу сказать, дефективные менеджеры делают свою работу. Успешно в игре добавляется, обновляется и балансится только донат (магазин). Я в любом случае периодически буду поигрывать в данную игру, может даже изменю как-то свое мнение, но, если честно, очень сильно в этом сомневаюсь. Уж слишком игра взяла большой угол падения на дно.

Всем желаю приятной игры.

The Battlefield I grew up with has turned into a product designed more around monetization than passion for the game itself. 

Older Battlefield titles had large-scale chaos that felt authentic and immersive. In Battlefield 6, the maps feel too small, too controlled, and too formulaic. Too often, it feels like two teams fighting over the same predictable central objectives again and again. Instead of natural sandbox chaos, the game tries to artificially force ''Battlefield moments.'' 
This becomes even more noticeable when older Battlefield maps like Firestorm return years later and somehow feel worse than they originally did. You'd expect a reused or copied map to at least maintain the same gameplay quality, if not improve upon it, not feel like a downgrade.

The monetization is terrible. Locking certain weapon and ''loadouts'' behind battle passes to give you earlier access to weapons that would require unlock requirements otherwise in a full price AAA game already feels wrong, but removing progression from previous battle passes when a new season starts is incredibly anti player. 
If I paid for a battle pass, I should be able to complete it at my own pace instead of losing access because a new season launched. I expected a system that allowed players to return to previous battle passes and finish progression they already paid for. That feels like basic fairness toward your player base, yet the game doesn't offer it.

Battlefield used to create trends. Now it feels like it's chasing them. Even the separate free-to-play battle royale game feels like Battlefield is trying to chase the success of Call of Duty rather than focusing on what originally made the franchise stand out. Battlefield used to have its own identity. Now parts of it feel designed around cosmetics and monetization systems instead of the classic sandbox warfare experience.

The industry used to rely on making great games that sold in high volumes through quality and reputation. Now many AAA studios like this one, release unfinished games at full price and expect players to wait years for the game to become what it should have been at launch. Yet somehow the in-game store, battle passes, skins and microtransactions are perfectly finished from day one in this game. That level of greed is hard to ignore.

Battlefield 6 feels uninspired, unfinished and more focused on retention systems and microtransactions than on delivering a memorable Battlefield experience. It used to set the standard for large-scale shooters. Now it feels like it's chasing trends while forgetting what made the franchise special in the first place. If this is what Battlefield has become, then I can no longer recommend it at all.

The most disappointing part is that I no longer have faith in DICE and EA to understand what made Battlefield unique. I hope that one day a new studio emerges and remembers that players want a great Battlefield game, not a storefront disguised as one.

Ребята, это фиаско. Я, как и миллионы других «лохов», купился на сладкие обещания EA в октябре 25-го. Нам обещали возвращение к истокам, тотальное разрушение и дух старой доброй Батлы. Трейлеры под знакомый ремикс сработали как идеальная доза ностальгии - и вот мы уже несем деньги в кассу.

А теперь сухие факты после полугода игры:

Онлайн - это просто катастрофа. На старте в Steam было 750 тысяч человек. Сейчас? Еле наскребаем 30-40 тысяч. Падение на 90%! Это не «плановый отток», это эвакуация.

Геймплей для снайперов и «крыс». Карты - это просто бесконечные пустые поля (Open Space). Если ты не в танке и не на вертолете, ты - мясо. Пехоте бежать некуда, тебя снимают с другого конца карты челики с дальномерами, которым даже баллистику учитывать не надо. Жмешь кнопку - фраг. Скука смертная.

Контентный голод. За три месяца нам выкатили аж... две карты. Зато магазин ломится от скинов. Приоритеты EA понятны: зачем чинить регистрацию попаданий или оптимизацию, если можно впарить очередной «Баттлпасс на воздух».
Массовые увольнения в марте 2026 года в ключевых студиях (DICE, Criterion) после «самого успешного старта в истории» — это верх цинизма. Пока разработчиков выставляют на улицу, нам предлагают предзаказывать баттлпасы 3-го сезона, даже не показывая их содержимое.

Цинизм зашкаливает. Смерть Винса Зампелы, который был последней надеждой на нормальную игру, они превратили в маркетинговый повод. Выпустили памятную нашивку и через неделю анонсировали новый сезон доната. Это просто мародерство.

Техническое состояние. Чем больше патчей, тем хуже играется. ФПС прыгает, регистрация попаданий живет своей жизнью. Игра ощущается как кривой клон Call of Duty, который потерял свое лицо, но так и не приобрел чужое.

The devs say promising things like adjusting controller's recoil reduction and time to kill, but the game is just so unfun. Tanks and vehicles everywhere to kill you, die instantly because you were spotted, and lose 1v1's because console players have aim assist and hit every shot, while mouse players have to suffer from recoil and precision. The attachment don't make sense, and 90% of the guns aren't viable.

It's just not a very good game. Nothing you do has impact or consequences.

> If you die, you can spawn almost instantly. There's little to no consequence of dying.
> Since this applies to enemies, there's little to no consequence to killing anyone or anything.
> Reviving is rarely useful because you can spawn anyway, and you get full ammo for it!
> You can spawn on teammates (if not in combat), so expect a 1 vs. 1 to randomly turn into a group battle because someone took cover for 2 seconds.
> You can spawn on vehicles, so expect contesting an area to be interesting when a vehicle rolls up, and suddely it's a group battle.
> Vehicles respawn in a minute. Hence, there's no impact of hunting and killing a vehicle.
> You heal to full health after 3 seconds, so there's no impact to getting hit.
> Hitting an enemy 6 times does not slow or impair them, so there's no consequence to being hit or mortally wounding someone.
> Guns are weird. Getting hit by a shotgun is a 1-hit kill. Getting hit by a 50.cal takes 2-3 shots to kill at least.
> Trades are rarely tactical - the one with the highest ROF wins.

Oh and let's not mention the bloat - the DLC, battle passes, packages, skins, etc.. It's just too much of everything, and nothing is really special or outstanding.

Two full seasons have gone by and casual players have essentially been abandoned.

No new casual playlists. No meaningful playlist updates. No experimentation with fun rotating modes. Nothing.

This is honestly one of the biggest frustrations with Battlefield 6 right now because it sends a very clear message: the casual side of the community is not a priority.

Not everyone wants to sweat in hyper-competitive matches 24/7. A huge part of what made Battlefield special over the years was hopping into fun, chaotic, lower-pressure playlists with friends and just enjoying the sandbox. That variety is what kept people playing for hundreds of hours.

Right now the playlist experience feels stale, repetitive, and neglected. Two seasons is MORE than enough time to add new casual experiences, rotate classic modes, test community favorites, or at the very least communicate what the plan is.

Silence is what makes this so frustrating.

The community keeps bringing this up because people CARE about the game and want it to succeed. But when feedback about casual playlists gets ignored season after season, it starts feeling like the dev team either doesn’t see the issue or simply doesn’t care.

Please stop treating casual content like an afterthought. Battlefield needs fun, social, replayable playlists just as much as it needs ranked balance and competitive tuning.

Right now, one entire side of the playerbase feels forgotten.

Written right at the end of Season 2. TLDR as a long time BF fan its around 3-3,5/5.

Positives:
- Audio design is absolutely sublime
- Gameplay overall is fun - decent selection of guns that are all fun, distinct, and great to use (secondaries suck tho). Attachment system is interesting and varied. Movement is grounded while still giving room for tech and skill expression. No egregious gadgets IMO. Neat teamwork additions that make you feel like an actual team without forcing anything.
- Art direction is pretty good (altho please let us turn off/adjust the color grading)
- Free battlepass grind isn't too bad even when you have a job and other games to play (FYI, not a fan of battlepasses either but gotta give credit where its due)
- Redsec Gauntlet is actually pretty damn fun and a neat addition
- Devs are decently responsive and communicative
- Performance is actually good

Meh
- Microtransactions are pretty annoying and the skins are mostly underwhelming anyway. At least you can ignore them?
- Bloated & uninteresting gamemode additions
- Vehicle gameplay is still kind of weird, but could be skill issue and the devs said they're going to improve things come Season 3. Could also be a map issue.

Bad
- Map count isn't great
- A lot of the maps aren't really well designed either IMO. How tf did they mess up Firestorm?? Visibility also sucks a lot in dim areas.
- Breakthrough & Rush suck
- Attachment grind is still bad even after patches
- UI/UX IS HORRIBLE. Never got used to it. Slow, clunky, and genuinely impedes your experience. Putting it not at terrible because its not a dealbreaker for me but goodness its ASS.
- Haven't really delved into Portal but so far seems like a missed opportunity yet again like in 2042

Terrible
- NO PERSISTENT SERVERS. Matchmaking & no server browser is already bad enough, but no persistent servers can genuinely kill your gaming session if you live in lower-populated regions.

Então vamos aos contras do jogo, e no final alguns prós se quiser mesmo jogar seu dinheiro fora nessa bomba.
Contras, (posso esquecer de alguns):
Lobbies cheios de bots.
Não tem server browser igual todos os BF's anteriores.
As armas parecem pouco potentes, com o som sendo completamente obliterado com um silenciador.
As armas do meta não possuem recuo, fazendo-a parecer sem peso e potência.
A movimentação do jogo é muito rápida e frenética, não tem nada haver com a franquia BF onde é mais lento e tático. O BF6 beneficia jogadores de COD.
O jogo é um cod-like.
Os blindados são feitos de papel, uma sanfonada e acabou o forró. Chuva de RPG.
O jogo não incentiva jogo em equipe, é cada um por si, médicos não revivem os aliados.
O jogo tem um filtro azul parecendo um filme do méxico invertido.
Os gráficos são simplórios demais apesar de seu peso excessivo em CPU e timing de RAM, a GPU quase dorme toda vez no jogo, não se compara com a otimização dos BF's antigos, como o BF1, BF4, Bad Company 2, BF3, e por aí vai. Minha RX 590 e Ryzen 5 4500 rodam BF1 a 100 fps no preset alto em 1080p nativo, já no BF6 pena pra rodar em 60 fps com tudo no mínimo, é uma vergonha a não-otimização que a DICE NÃO fez nesse jogo.
Muitas micro-transações que nunca existiram na franquia BF antes, skins que ninguém quer e passes de batalhas forçados nos players.
Muitos desafios sem sentido.
As armas demoram uma eternidade pra upar.
Pouca variedade de arma de classe pra classe, as SMG podem muito bem ser usadas em classe de assalto, e sniper ou ML, ou rifles serem usados em engenheiro, etc, o jogo não incentiva armas class-bound.
O time-to-kill é muito baixo, você mal vê um player e ele já te vaporizou em meio segundo, na franquia BF anteriormente as armas não importam muito, elas te davam pouca pra nenhuma vantagem, e os acessórios eram puramente pra melhorar alguns aspectos da gameplay (laser/luneta/bocal), agora no BF6 é puramente quebrado uma arma full acessório do meta (não tem sway vertical/horizontal, mobilidade e velocidade de Hermes da mitologia grega e TTK de 1seg).
Battle-royale, (isso já fala por si só).
Modos que ninguém joga por não ser interessante ou não ter incentivo por parte do estúdio.
Preço absurdo, sim, é um TRIPLE AAA, mas isso é pura ganância corporativa e não vale nem um centavo, por isso o REDSEC existe.

Os veículos não são nada realistas, tanto em física quanto em modelagem.

O jogo é um live-service em sua essência, mas acaba virando um limitado, pois demorou mais de 6 meses pra lançar uma nova season (Season 2), e com ela veio só umas coisas mequetrefe que não justificam +6 meses de espera, além de vários problemas estruturais que nunca foram consertados, como o NetCode ruim (que impacta no seu registro de tiros, sincronização com servidor pra física do jogo, conexão com servidores, etc), má otimização de CPU (se baseando fortemente em single-core invés de multi-core), ausência de tecnologia de frame-skip pra evitar que o jogo fique em câmera lenta por CPU Overload, então muitos jogadores com CPUs mais fracas (que convenhamos, não são tão ruins assim), experienciem o jogo em câmera lenta ou travadas frequentes, tudo por falta de otimização.

Dito isso, agora vem os prós, que todo jogo possui mas esse aqui em específico é difícil dizer.
Prós:
Battlefield mais recente, (deixando certo frescor pros fãs da franquia).
Mapas até-que-bonitos, falta verticalidade pra maioria mas é algo a se considerar.
É divertido explodir coisas no jogo.
A direção de arte dos sons do jogo é bem feita, apesar de ter o problema de não conseguirmos identificar aliado de inimigo pelo som, ainda sim as gravações de guerra são muito bem feitas, a dublagem também tá decente.
A animação das armas tá até que boa se for comparar com outros FPS's.
A estética futurista dos menus e animações de HUD são interessantes, a distribuição dos elementos no HUD também são legais.

Mas são essas as coisas boas que posso falar do jogo, por que não inovou em nada a franquia BF, tentaram reinventar a roda, não aceitaram que o que funcionava era pra continuar igual, e acabaram criando esse amalgamado de ♥♥♥♥♥ que imita Battlefield.
Eu realmente me sinto muito mal pela DICE entregar algo tão cagado pro público, eles podiam ter feito melhor se não fosse a ganância e idiotice da EA, poderíamos realmente ter algo novo e revolucionário, mas acho que é aqui que traçamos a linha do fim da franquia Battlefield, aproveitem pra jogar os BF's antigos, como o 1 e o 4 até que eles caiam em esquecimento e só sobre essa ♥♥♥♥♥ de BF6. I think this game is a faster-paced, more balanced iteration of Battlefield 4, and although I prefer the slower gameplay of 4, I still find this one a lot of fun, and in a lot of cases, I find to be even better.

Positives aside, the game has some downsides, some worse than others:

- The netcode is genuinely bad, and it is the worst technical aspect of the game. It needs to be fixed immediately.

- Lack of content compared to other Battlefield games.*

- Mind-bogglingly confusing and aggressive microtransactions that infest the battlepass and the store.

- Lack of cool set-pieces/levolution. Even though there is an element of player destruction in the game, it's very lackluster and not as cool or match-changing as those of the older games. A huge miss, in my opinion.

- The campaign is the worst one out of the entire series. I cannot do it justice to describe how bad it is; you will just have to take my word for it. The plot is nonsensical (to the point it impacts the setting and feeling you're playing in the MP), the characters are forgettable, levels are bad and generic, and the writing is poor. The whole campaign feels like they looked at MW2019 and went "That did well, we should copy it, but put our own spin on it!" then they never really commited to making their own spin on it, and then they rushed it. One of the most unenjoyable gaming experiences I've had in recent memory.

*The content in this game would suffice if it had to stand on its own two legs, but I still don't think that's an excuse worthy of a publisher and developer such as EA and Co. Although I am looking forward to the new content, as it would make an already great experience better.

Overall, I think this is an actual good and fun game that gets a bit too much hate for my understanding, especially as a newcomer to this entry specifically. If the game fixed the netcoding, pulled back on the aggressive monetization, and added a bit more content, it would probably be my personal favorite Battlefield, perhaps even surpassing 4 and 1.

And this doesn't factor into my review, but the community is unusually aggressive and, frankly, stupid when compared to other FPS communities. Don't expect the chat to be used for anything but toxicity, and don't expect either your team or the enemy to be particularly smart or capable. I don't know what's in the water for the community to be this insufferable.

Общее впечатление: Возвращение величия (почти без оговорок)
DICE наконец-то услышала фанатов. После провала Battlefield 2042, шестая часть ощущается как долгожданное возвращение корням. Это брутальный, современный шутер, который сочетает хардкорный дух старых частей (BF3/BF4) с современными технологиями. Да, есть шероховатости (стоит помнить про скандалы со скинами и нестабильные серверы на релизе ), но геймплейная база здесь — золото. Теперь по пунктам.

1. Атмосферный ультиматум: Звук стрельбы и взрывов
Звуковой дизайн в BF6 — это, пожалуй, лучшее, что я слышал в шутерах за последние 5 лет. Разработчики проделали титаническую работу, чтобы поле боя "ожило".

Стрельба с характером: Каждый ствол звучит уникально. Штурмовая винтовка выдает сочный, механический лязг затвора, пулемет гудит басовитым металлическим рокотом, а снайперка оглушает хлопком, от которого закладывает уши даже на расстоянии . В настройках категорически рекомендую включить пресет "War Tapes" (или его злую версию V.A.L.). Этот режим убирает "киношную" обработку и добавляет жесткости, дисторшена и агрессии — ощущение, будто вы находитесь внутри бочки с патронами .

Физика взрывов: Взрывы раскатистые. Когда работает артиллерия или залетает авиационный удар по небу, низкие частоты разносятся по наушникам так, что в груди вибрирует. Особенно радует эффект приглушенности звука, если рядом разорвался снаряд ("звон в ушах").

Приоритеты (апдейт Winter Offensive): В свежих патчах разработчики исправили старую проблему с "кашей" из звуков . Теперь шаги врагов или звук перезарядки не тонут в общем хаосе войны, но при этом глобальный эпос разрушений никуда не делся.

2. Оружейный оргазм: Приятная и честная стрельба
Это именно то место, где BF6 остановилась в шаге от идеала, но споткнулась о "полировку". Тем не менее, стрелять объективно приятно.

Ощущение мощи: Оружие в руках чувствуется как тяжелый инструмент убийства. Анимации перезарядки плавные и детализированные.

Проблема с отдачей (Почти лазеры): Тут есть нюанс. Многие ветераны жалуются, что отдача слишком маленькая, а пули летят слишком точно (особенно с контроллера из-за ассиста). Это немного упрощает скилл и делает перестрелки менее "штурмовыми", чем в BF3 .

Но! Если вы новичок или пришли из более казуальных шутеров — вам понравится. Оружие слушается, пули не улетают в небо через три выстрела.

Разрушаемость: Стрельба становится приятнее благодаря тому, что окружение реагирует. Пули пробивают тонкие стены, оставляют кратеры, а из-за вашей очереди на точке начинает сыпаться штукатурка. Это добавляет тактильной кайфа к самому процессу нажатия на курок .

3. Игровая вселенная: Актуальные режимы на любой вкус
Набор режимов в BF6 — это идеальный баланс между масштабным безумием и киберспортивной динамикой.

Для любителей больших войн (эпик и тактика):
Здесь всё серьезно. Режимы Conquest (на 64 игрока) и Breakthrough (48 игроков) — это сердце игры. Чтобы победить, нужна командная работа на технике (карты огромные), координация отрядов и использование классов . В режиме "Эскалация" (Escalation) точки захвата постоянно смещаются, не давая игрокам засесть в "окопах" .

Для быстрых перестрелок (тем, кто не любит бегать 5 минут):
Если нет времени на "эпик", режимы просто спасают ситуацию:

Командный бой насмерть (Team Deathmatch): Урезано всё лишнее (техника, огромные расстояния). Только мясо, углы и стволы. 16 на 16, быстрые матчи до 100 фрагов .

Squad Deathmatch и Domination: Идеально для разогрева или игры соло. Компактные карты, минимум тактики, максимум динамики. Очень заходит, когда нужно выбить челлендж на оружие .

Rush: Возвращение легенды! Из-за того, что режим завязан на постановке бомб, здесь гораздо больше концентрации дыма, гранат и ближнего боя, чем в обычном "Захвате" .

Вердикт
Battlefield 6 — это тот случай, когда хочется закрыть глаза на технические недочеты (редкие баги или спорные моменты с балансом дробовиков ) ради чистого геймплейного удовольствия.
Звук качает, бегать и стрелять весело, а выбор режима позволяет либо вкатиться на часок в "Team Deathmatch", либо зависнуть до ночи в эпичных осадах "Breakthrough". Однозначно рекомендую к покупке, если соскучились по хорошему, злому и технологичному Battlefield.

A solid start that fizzled out, the focus of development on cosmetics prevents the game to truly shine. Each battlefield game got more re-playable as time went on because they added new maps which made it fun to play again. The maps in BF6 are small and barren between points forcing combat only on the points you need to capture. Fights become predictable which causes two issues: it becomes boring for veteran players since they know the meta spots and difficult for newer players as they get killed often until they switch their tactics to the former leading to the same problem. The counter-point to this is the "levelution" they added into the game but underneath all the destructible areas (which is really a small number of them) its just barren terrain that leads to even more boring fights if you exploit the destructible environment. For $70 USD it really should give more re-playability, especially with all these operations and the battle-pass they want to add. Granted it is an obvious cash grab since its basically just cosmetics but why would buy the battle-pass if the game gets boring after a couple of weeks of playing it? It makes no sense. The challenges to unlock items are also tedious and uninspired. Whereas other previous titles required varied gameplay to unlock or use other classes, BF6 challenges are often completed by playing the class as you normally would. It doesn't feel earned, its just "oh neat...anyway..." then you continue playing as you normally do. Honestly, you might feel more "pride and accomplishment" unlocking things the way they had it back in 2017, iykyk. With extremely slow development of new maps and a poor progression system it's not worth investing into. Don't buy it. Just play BF4, honestly.

[h1]Battlefield 6 — Tesão balístico com pedigree[/h1]

Há jogos que entretêm. Há jogos que ocupam espaço no SSD. Há jogos que existem para vender passe de batalha e produzir notificações.

E há [b]Battlefield 6[/b].

Depois de [b]309 horas[/b], já não existe mais a fase do “estou testando”. Ninguém joga 309 horas por educação. O jogo ou te captura, ou você desinstala e segue a vida como um cidadão funcional. No meu caso, Battlefield 6 me capturou com a delicadeza de uma artilharia caindo no telhado.

E eu agradeço.

Battlefield sempre foi minha franquia preferida, mas BF6 fez algo que eu já não esperava com tanta força: ele me devolveu uma sensação antiga. Aquela memória viva dos melhores tempos de [b]Battlefield 4[/b], quando cada partida parecia menos uma rodada de videogame e mais uma história absurda sendo escrita no meio da fumaça, do concreto quebrado e da mais pura incompetência coletiva transformada em glória.

BF6 não é perfeito. Mas quando acerta, ele acerta com gosto.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]O retorno do velho caos[/h2]

O que Battlefield 6 faz de melhor é lembrar que Battlefield nunca foi só sobre matar inimigos. É sobre [b]estar dentro de uma guerra grande demais para você controlar[/b], mas aberta o bastante para você deixar sua marca.

Um tanque muda a frente de combate. Um prédio destruído altera a leitura do mapa. Um squad minimamente coordenado parece uma unidade de elite. Um squad comum parece quatro primatas armados tentando fundar uma doutrina militar. Ambos são Battlefield. Ambos são belíssimos.

E no meio disso tudo, existe o prazer quase indecente de encontrar seu papel no caos.

No meu caso: rifle de longo alcance, paciência e intenção.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]O prazer do tiro bem dado[/h2]

Battlefield 6 entende o ritual do sniper.

Não é só mirar e clicar. É ler o mapa. Antecipar movimento. Escolher posição. Sentir a distância. Compensar o tempo. Esperar o erro do inimigo como quem aguarda uma confissão.

Então vem o disparo.

[b]Seco. Pesado. Limpo.[/b]

A bala cruza o espaço, encontra o alvo, e o som do headshot estala no ouvido como uma pequena bênção profana.

É difícil explicar com sobriedade. Então não vou fingir: [b]é delicioso[/b].

Cada tiro bem colocado em BF6 tem uma textura própria. As armas têm corpo. O som tem presença. O impacto tem consequência. O jogo entende que áudio não é enfeite; é parte do prazer. Explosões, cápsulas, concreto, motores, tiros distantes, o grave de um blindado, o assobio de munição passando perto demais — tudo trabalha para colocar o jogador naquele estado mental raro em que o mundo real dá uma educada sumida.

Por alguns minutos, só existe o campo de batalha.

E talvez uma vítima a 200 metros achando que estava segura. Coitada. A geometria discordou.

[hr][/hr]

O áudio de Battlefield 6 merece menção própria. Este jogo não apenas soa bem; ele [b]respira guerra[/b].

O som das armas é encorpado. As explosões têm peso. Os ambientes têm profundidade. Os headshots têm aquele estalo criminosamente satisfatório que deveria vir com advertência sanitária.

É um deleite para quem joga de fone. Um deleite perigoso. O tipo de som que faz você querer jogar “só mais uma” até perceber que o relógio já avançou como uma ofensiva inimiga.

Battlefield sempre soube fazer barulho. BF6 sabe fazer música com o barulho.

Música brutal, evidentemente. Mas música.

[hr][/hr]

BF6 é divertido. Escandalosamente divertido. Aquele tipo de divertido que faz você xingar uma morte injusta e apertar “jogar de novo” antes mesmo de terminar a reclamação. O tipo de jogo que ainda consegue gerar histórias. O tipo de multiplayer que, mesmo não sendo perfeito, entrega momentos que justificam a noite inteira.

E isso, hoje, não é pouco.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Veredito[/h2]

Battlefield 6 é o retorno de uma sensação que parecia meio perdida.

Ele resgata memórias de BF4, mas não vive apenas delas. Ele entrega gunplay forte, áudio espetacular, caos em larga escala e aquela liberdade clássica da franquia: a liberdade de jogar sério, jogar taticamente, jogar como um completo animal ou alternar entre os três no intervalo de trinta segundos.

Depois de 309 horas, meu veredito é simples:
[h3]Battlefield 6 é Battlefield de verdade.[/h3]

Falho, barulhento, às vezes teimoso, às vezes irritante — mas vivo. Intenso. Gostoso. Brutal. Divertido de um jeito que poucos shooters modernos ainda conseguem ser.

E quando aquele tiro perfeito atravessa o mapa, encontra o capacete inimigo e o som do headshot estala no ouvido…

[b]não é só nostalgia.[/b]
[h2]É tesão balístico com pedigree.[/h2]

❌ NON RECOMMANDÉ

Ancien joueur de BF3 BF4, BF1 BF5 et même 2042 (qui est un chef-d'œuvre à côté de cette purge), je suis sur le cul. DICE a réussi l’exploit de sortir un jeu en 2026 qui est moins beau, moins lisible et moins bien optimisé que des titres sortis il y a 8 ans.

LES POINTS QUI TUENT LE JEU :

Visibilité honteuse : On est en 2026, j'ai une 7900 XTX et un écran 165 Hz, et j'ai l'impression d'avoir de la vaseline sur l'écran. Le jeu force des filtres de flou (Weapon DOF, TAA immonde) qui rendent les duels à distance illisibles. Même en tweakant les fichiers config, le moteur Frostbite s'obstine à flouter les côtés de l'écran. C’est fatigant nerveusement et injouable pour un joueur compétitif.

Maps de campeurs : Ils ont confondu "complexe" et "labyrinthe". Trop de recoins, trop de verticalité inutile, aucune ligne de front claire. L'essence de Battlefield (le jeu agressif et le mouvement) est morte. Tu te fais punir instantanément par un mec caché dans un amas de débris indétectable. Le TTK est devenu tellement punitif qu'on n'a plus aucune chance de "outplay" en cas de duel.

Optimisation à la ramasse : Mon i5-12600K est à genoux alors qu'il n'y a aucune raison. La destruction "réaliste" sacrifie tout le reste. Résultat : des textures de sol et de murs qui font pitié par rapport à un BF1 ou un BF5. C’est un gâchis de ressources monumental.

Conclusion :
Si vous voulez jouer à Battlefield, réinstallez BF5 pour l'ambiance et la destruction, ou 2042 pour le fun moderne. Si vous voulez un vrai jeu de guerre actuel, allez sur Delta Force. Mais fuyez ce BF6 qui n'est qu'un simulateur de frustration flou et mal conçu. DICE a perdu la boussole.

Wer eine schnelle und stabile Internetverbindung hat, wird in Battlefield 6 paradoxerweise bestraft. Die technische Umsetzung des Spiels (Netcode/Lag Compensation) ist eine absolute Katastrophe für jeden, der kompetitives Gameplay erwartet.
Das Spiel bevorzugt aktiv Spieler mit schlechten Leitungen. Man stirbt regelmäßig eine volle Sekunde, nachdem man bereits hinter einer massiven Mauer in Deckung gegangen ist.
Man schießt Gegnern direkt ins Gesicht, aber die Treffer werden nicht gewertet, während der Gegner einen Sekundenbruchteil später mit wenigen Schüssen erledigt. (Instant Death).
Es ist keine Seltenheit, Spieler mit Pings von über 2000 ms auf den Servern zu sehen.
Anstatt diese Spieler zu kicken, wird das gesamte Match-Erlebnis für alle anderen durch die Synchronisationsversuche des Servers zerstört.
Es fühlt sich an, als ob EA die technische Qualität opfert, um niemanden mit einer schlechten Leitung zu benachteiligen. Wer 70 Euro für ein Spiel ausgibt und eine moderne Glasfaserleitung besitzt, sollte keinen Nachteil gegenüber Spielern mit instabilem Internet haben. Für mich war das definitiv das letzte Battlefield.

Ou você cai com um squad tático nível forças especiais…
ou com 3 caras olhando parede e um sniper 4km longe do objetivo.

Great at launch as with all live service games there has been a significant decline in playerbase due to the shift in the gaming landscape but also DICE dropping the ball in terms of updates and quality of life updates. 

When it comes to performance I'm still new to PC gaming (outside of low spec indies and mobas) I've had varying success keeping my framerate above 120fps 1440p without the use of DLSS. DLSS helps but I'm a complete scrub and learning how to optimize my experience given my machine. 

Class wise the game does feel unbalanced. Nice change from beta to give assualt the spawn beacon but I hate the fact the stim injector is only a CC cleanse instead of boosting healing rate in other games. Maybe I'm out of touch with what the devs and community expect. 

Support does its job and there was an issue at launch with the large influx of players being new not understanding the importance of reviving and healing. It's been fixed with the player base that remains. 

Engineer is my least played class so I can't comment too much 

Recon does the job of giving info and taking out people at a distance. My major gripe has been the sweet spot mechanic (getting 1 shot in specific ranges in the upper torso) but I can see why the devs put it in differentiate the sniper rifles. Also I see the split between the community of older players putting an emphasis  on getting headshots which can be difficult at range if you don't know what you are doing. 

I play the game on a Dualsense controller and have enjoyed my time playing. Very rarely do I play mouse and key only if my controller is dead or somewhere else that I'm too lazy to grab it. 

One last thing..... the campaign, is hot garbage if you expecting the same quality of campaign from previous BattleField games or even some of the decent Call of Duty campaigns. Just play it to get whatever outfits you want rewards from it. It is really that bad. There are articles out there you can find that there was a lot of turmoil to even get the campaign done apparently. 

In all decent game 7.5/10 from a casual who mostly played BattleField 1. There have been fixes and from what I understand DICE doing DICE things of being late to the party for fixes. I suggest if you want this game pick it up on a deep sale and or wait till the game is has been out for a year which seems to be the sentiment of Battlefield players who played previous games.

Not a hardcore Battlefield guy but I've been playing Battlefield here and there since BF3. BFV was my favorite previous game but I've also had lots of fun in BF4. I just grabbed it on sale lately because some buddies were playing it and I've been having a blast. This is the first time a Battlefield game gripped me like this.

The gunplay feels really nice once you figure out how to build the guns for your playstyle (i.e. for me I really value ADS accuracy while moving because I like to strafe in gunfights like CoD). I really like the open weapons since it makes me actually wanna run other classes than my go-to assault and try out other gadgets. I always like to run ARs (and sometimes carbines) in my Battlefield games because I like being effective at close to mid range. Well, I'm no longer locked to the Assault class, and nobody is stopping me from running my ARs on Recon (and lucky I can do that, because the assault class lowkey kinda sucks). Still though, some class boosts for the guns are so significant that I don't really wanna run LMGs outside of Support and I don't wanna run Snipers outside of Recon.

People say the maps suck. I'm kinda fine on most of them, but also I don't play Conquest much but rather Breakthrough and Rush. There's some objectives that are real stinkers (the first set of objectives if you're attacking on the Blackwell Oil Fields map, for example) but otherwise they play fine in my opinion.

Not sure where people are having this idea of keyboard and mouse players getting dumped on by aimbot-like aim assist on controllers. The guns in this game have almost no recoil except for a select few with high recoil as their key downside. I hold my own just find on keyboard and mouse and I occasionally am among the top players on my team. Build your guns for low bloom, move that mouse down a bit while shooting, and maybe even tap fire a bit.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]✅ Was gut funktioniert[/h2]

[b]Waffen-Feeling, das überzeugt[/b]
Jede Waffe hat ihren eigenen Charakter. Das Gunplay sitzt, die Rückstoßmuster fühlen sich durchdacht an und das Treffen befriedigender Ziele macht auch nach vielen Stunden noch Spaß.

[b]Destruktion & Fahrzeuge auf Battlefield-Niveau[/b]
Hier steckt die Seele der Reihe. Ein Panzerturm, der durch eine Kettenreaktion abgesprengt wird und dabei einen Helikopter vom Himmel holt. Eine Mine, die einem Gegner in der Hand hochgeht, weil man sie angeschossen hat. Diese Momente passieren, sie sind nicht geskriptet – und genau das macht Battlefield aus.

[b]Grafik & Atmosphäre[/b]
Die Schlachtfelder sehen beeindruckend aus. Rauch, Staub, Explosionen – die visuelle Dichte zieht einen ins Geschehen hinein. Der Sound tut sein Übriges: Wer mit Kopfhörern spielt, ist mittendrin.

[b]Technisch solide[/b]
Die Performance hält, was sie verspricht. Stabile Frameraten, gute Grafikoptionen – auf dieser Seite gibt es wenig zu meckern.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]❌ Was stört[/h2]

[b]Zu wenig Maps[/b]
Die vorhandenen Karten sind gut gestaltet, aber es sind schlicht zu wenige. Wer viel spielt, kennt jede Ecke auswendig schneller als einem lieb ist.

[b]Balancing braucht noch Arbeit[/b]
Manche Fahrzeuge, Klassen oder Waffen sind spürbar stärker als andere. Das kippt gelegentlich ganze Runden – und das frustriert, wenn man auf der falschen Seite dieser Gleichung steht.

[b]Netcode & Server[/b]
Der größte Wermutstropfen: Verbindungsprobleme und ein unzuverlässiger Netcode trüben das Erlebnis regelmäßig. Treffer, die nicht registriert werden, oder Aussetzer im entscheidenden Moment – das darf bei einem reinen Multiplayer-Titel schlicht nicht passieren.

[hr][/hr]

[i]Battlefield 6 ist dann am besten, wenn es sich selbst treu bleibt: chaotisch, laut, unvorhersehbar und voller Momente, die kein anderes Spiel so hinbekommt. Die technischen Schwächen nerven – aber sie können dieses Gefühl nicht vollständig zerstören.[/i]

Netcode is overall terrible. I notice being shot behind cover multiple times a match.

These reasons are so impactful to the experience, they are sufficient enough to force me to recommend you steer clear of this game.

It's a shame, because the core shooting gameplay, and graphics are cool (it's Battlefield). If they actually got the netcode right, it would be a decent enough BF game, but still with it's issues. I have always loved BF, I first played when BF3 came out. Thought they'd learned their lesson as the beta actually ran graphically smoothly, but my mistake - seems like EA would rather rush the game out the door and fix it over time.

Further issues,

Not many big maps. Even on the small amount of maps that are big, they are often too sparse for how many players are on them. This often leads to getting caught out in the open with little to no cover, and getting shot from multiple different angles. Whereas, on smaller maps the flow of the game is underlined by crowded choke points, constant suppression, and many many nades.

Skin customisation leads to confusing target identification. The beta was better in this regard simply because both teams had set uniforms. It's annoying to be flicking to a soldier on your screen only for his nametag to pop up because they're a teammate rather than an enemy. This could be fixed if there was a toggle feature that turned off and on skins. Speaking of which...

Game is way over-monetized. £70 game that has a seasonal battlepass, skins, and "Pro" version. The DLC system we had during BF3 and BF4 was a far better deal for players. EA being hyper-greedy as usual.


I'm waiting to see if they actually fix the netcode. If they fix it (which it should've been on release), then I will likely spend a lot more time in the game. At the moment, the overall experience is good at best, frustrating at worse.

The sound design is hauntingly authentic, the scale is immense, and the gameplay constantly balances all-out chaos with tactical teamwork.

Playing the beta for Battlefield 6 honestly felt like a breath of fresh air at first. The gunplay felt cleaner and more grounded, and for a moment it seemed like the series was getting back on track.

But the more I played, the more it started to feel repetitive. Matches fall into the same loop over and over, and that sense of chaos and variety that older Battlefield games had just isn’t hitting the same here.

The guns don’t really help either. A lot of them feel pretty generic, and the attachments don’t add much personality or meaningful difference to how they play. It ends up making progression feel less rewarding than it should.

Visually, the game looks good, but it also feels kind of generic. It doesn’t have that grit or atmosphere that made games like Battlefield 1 stand out. Everything feels a bit too clean, and it loses some of that raw, immersive edge because of it.

It also feels like the focus has shifted more toward revenue systems than the actual gameplay experience. That doesn’t completely ruin it, but it does make the game feel a bit hollow after a while.

At this point, I can’t really recommend the game. It has a solid foundation, but it needs a lot more depth and variety to stay engaging long-term.

Battlefield Studios and Vince Zampella, the guy behind the original Modern Warfare and Titanfall, came in after 2042 and basically rebuilt the series from the ground up with Battlefield 3 and 4 as the north star. The result is the most polished large scale multiplayer shooter in years, proper classes back, tactical destruction, 64 player battles that feel like actual chaos rather than organized chaos, and sound design that genuinely has no business being as good as it is. The audio alone is worth talking about. Jets tearing overhead, tank shells breaking the sound barrier, it's the kind of thing headphones were invented for.

The maps have been a legitimate complaint and the player count dropped heading into 2026 because of it. DICE has acknowledged it and the roadmap looks promising with Wake Island returning and naval warfare coming back, but the slow content rollout is a fair gripe from people who wanted more out of the gate.

[h1] We reviewed your money and didn’t take any action this time [/h1]
I hadn’t played the "Battlefield" series in a long time before this game.
Because "BF1" was too demanding on my computer.
Because "BF5" is a piece of crap.
Because "BF2042" turned out to be a disappointment.
So when BF6 came out, I was really excited and invited a lot of my friends to play and buy the game... [b]Well, sorry for pushing you to spend money on this crap from EA.[/b]

[h3] So what made me fail to realize that this game is total garbage, and why did I spend over 380 hours on it? [/h3]
First of all, the game’s visuals are superb: the explosions are stunning and the models are interesting, and at first, a lot goes unnoticed behind that beautiful facade. 
Second, it brings back memories of how awesome it was to play BF4 and BF2.

[h3]So what's wrong with this game?[/h3]
[b] Everything else:  [/b]
[u] The reporting system: [/u] - You can report any profanity in a player’s nickname, and nothing will happen. You’ll get a generic response with no specifics. Maybe this system works for cheaters? No. EA claims they have almost no cheaters (90+% fair games), but you’ll never know if you died because of a cheater or because of a ping that decided to report that your opponent shot you before you came around the corner.
[u] Hit detection: [/u] Have you ever shot at Neo? Point-blank with a machine gun? And what happened next? Most likely, you died. And this happens all the time. You might start shooting 1–2 seconds too early, and your opponent will kill you. Why? Just because.
The same thing happens the other way around, but rarely. You hear a burst of gunfire behind you, turn around, and after another 1–2 seconds, you realize it’s not an ally but an enemy, so you click the mouse. The enemy is dead, but my character’s HP is still at 100%, even though the distance between us was less than 10–15 meters.
[u] Spawning on a control point or an ally. [/u]
Very often, the game spawns you right where the enemy is. Dying because you spawned right in front of an enemy APC is a classic scenario. The same thing happens if you spawn right in front of enemy players. 
[u] Vehicles: [/u]
The firing range for tanks and APCs is limited to 1 km; beyond that, shells lose their velocity very quickly. Therefore, it is impossible to use vehicles to flush out a sniper from a position deep in the rear of their base. Using aircraft is the solution, but there’s something odd about it in this game. The enemy’s air defense destroys all your aircraft with striking accuracy, while your missiles won’t lock onto anything. Many times, when flying directly at the enemy or keeping them within the range of a portable anti-aircraft missile system, the game tells you, “No, you can’t do that.” But you could be shot down far beyond the range of those missiles.
[u] Season Pass: [/u]
Unlike many others, I actually liked the character skins; they might be a bit odd, but they often do the job and don’t make the player stand out against the background. However, the rest of these passes are extremely poorly designed. They’re aimed at milking players for money by granting quick access to overpowered weapons.
[u] Maps: [/u]
Visually, they're beautiful, but they're unplayable. The new maps are even worse than the previous ones. After 50 hours of gameplay, they get old, and you end up repeating the same actions over and over. The classic “Capture” mode has turned into a battle between spawn campers and roofers. Escalation mode saved the game a bit, but there’s still an imbalance at various locations.
[u]Cross-play: [/u]
Whoever came up with the idea that PC players would enjoy playing against console players—with their forced auto-aim—clearly hated their job, because PC players can’t turn this cross-play feature off.
[u] REDSEC: [/u]
Why did you do that?

[h3] To summarize: [/h3]
DICE created a visually stunning game, but it was ruined by marketers and poor game design decisions. It was very sad to hear about the layoffs of the art team because they did an excellent job.

Made for casuals. Shoot-outs are geared towards "who saw who first" because the TTK is around 0,3s. The gameplay doesn't reward teamplay, strategy or good aim. It feels like the devs took away anything that could possibly bore you out by fear that you would go play something else.

I really wanted to like this, but I can’t recommend it. 

The biggest issue for me is how [b]casualized[/b] the gameplay feels. Large-scale FPS games thrive on depth, team coordination, meaningful roles, and rewarding mechanical skill. Here, most of that seems stripped away in favor of a faster, more accessible experience. That might appeal to some players, but it [b]comes at the cost of what makes this genre engaging long-term[/b].

A big part of that comes from the gunplay design. The [b]time-to-kill (TTK) is extremely fast[/b], but instead of making fights intense, it just makes them feel shallow. [b]It’s often just “who saw who first”[/b]. That gets even worse because visibility itself becomes part of the problem. There’s so much visual clutter that you’re pushed to lower your graphical settings to spot enemies faster. [b]The game is beautiful[/b] but that works against you greatly. 

What really kills the skill ceiling though, is the extremely low headshot multiplier. In most cases, landing headshots barely reduces the number of bullets needed to kill. You can hit multiple headshots and still need almost the same number of shots as if you were aiming at the body. That completely removes the incentive to aim well. The result is a system where skill is de-emphasized, and engagements feel random. 

Combine that with the overall chaotic flow of matches, and you end up with gameplay that lacks both tactical depth and individual impact. Instead of coordinated pushes or skill-based duels, [b]it’s mostly a loop of spawning, running, and trading kills with little consequence[/b].

If you’re looking for a laid-back, pick-up-and-play shooter, you might enjoy it. But if you value depth, precision, and the kind of skill expression that large-scale FPS games used to reward, this will likely feel shallow and underwhelming. 

Right now, it feels less like a game built around depth or mastery, and more like something designed to keep you constantly engaged, prioritizing attention retention over meaningful gameplay.

I have to admit, I have been too hard on Battlefield at times. I hated BF4 and not even Amy Hennig could save Hardline's singleplayer for me. I, also, thought that Battlefield 2042 was a huge misstep in the series in virtually every way while it was still a pretty playable game. Battlefield 6, I assumed very early on, was going to be still a few meters behind in terms of taking steps ahead, but I was going to be happy it would go into the right direction regardless.

I played the BF6 beta and I actually really enjoyed it. So naturally, I actually really do like BF6 even though I do not intend to play it in anything but a casual compacity. It is definitely not my "daily driver" game, as I have subsequently moved onto playing single player games almost exclusively. Not only that, but I actually do care about the campaign of milslop games and I had to find out if BF6 fumbled it as hard as my friends said it did.

Honestly, I think this is probably the best campaign in the modern era since BF3. And I really love BF3, while also hating BF4's campaign. There are definitely a lot of elements of this campaign that were silly, but I actually think it wrapped everything up in a believable way that solved a lot of my initial issues. The campaign itself is a lot of fun. It has some fantastic set pieces and the most dull parts are the ones that are simply too rural and not urban enough. There are some people who complain about the tighter urban combat, but I honestly think Battlefield excels at this better than most could ever dream. 

The nostalgia goggles of Battlefield fans are more like welding goggles, blocking the light from all else that is different from what we all played in our teenage years. I definitely get it, I remember coming home from school to dump dozens of hours into Bad Company 2 and its Vietnam expansion. I still remember getting underneath the park with a prone crawl glitch in BF3 beta, I still remember the red dot sight and UMP45 meta of that beta. Operation Metro Conquest is still the greatest MP game experience I ever had, having World War 3 over a ticket counter and having intense exchanges of small arms fire and munition exchange on staircaise or from down the hall. 

I also remember Project Reality Battlefield 2 and the Omnicide mods. I have forgotten more about Battlefield than most people could ever know, it is just that my steam account doesn't reflect the real hours I have put into these games. I remember playing Battlefield 1 at internet cafes in Copenhagen, Denmark with a bunch of Syrian dudes, guzzling Monster energy and halal hotdogs and kebab pizza. 

So... I am surprised that I actually thought BF6 was a lot of fun. Multiplayer wise, it still has iconic moments that cannot be replicated anywhere else. Scooting a house chair as concealment during a three way exchange of fire in a cramped back alley, narrowly dodging a destroyed helicopter's charred, metal corpse as it crushed several floors of the building around me, driving a jeep up close to the enemy's base, only to hop onto the gun and mow down thirty some people like Audie Murphy. Whether it is clutching a game solo as a medic or head shotting someone with a pistol as an engineer, or plinking hundreds of men down from behind enemy lines as a recon, the game is still Battlefield. 

And it is Battlefield in a grounded setting with a near peer enemy. 

But above all, it has urban cities. The WW1 and WW2 games served these developers well in creating rubble littered arenas of infantry and technical combat, but also building believable and lived in spaces. While I certainly think that environmentally, BF1 and BFV have some major victory points, the scale and spectacular presentation of the urban environments, complete with the current model of gameplay, makes Battlefield 6 very, very good. No longer is Battlefield fully taking steps forward and backwards in a strange slow dance of fate, but it is certainly side stepping along in a crab walk. Its not always effective or pretty to observe, but it shows they are moving toward greatness. 

The things that hold Battlefield back are the conventions of modern gaming and multiplayer. It is hard to really press the developers for doing what is necessary to keep a game topical and modern. Too great of a departure and you basically have a dead game on your hands or one that is doomed to not generate enough revenue to make a superior one better. 

Like I said, its not a Battlefield you may want to devote your life to like the old days of our teenhood recreational years, but its definitely a great game for hopping in for a few hours sometimes. 

Everyone really hated on the campaign this year and while its true that at times, it was a bit too generic and borrowed far too many entire sections from Battlefield 3, I still found it to be very playable. It lacks the emotional and at times, surprisingly great storytelling in BF1 and BFV, but in the same hand, it also avoided a lot of those campaign's critical mistakes. 

I think tanks control terribly in this game, however. To the point I feel they are just utterly meant to be unfun to discourage tank spam and camping, which was one of the abominable horrors of Battlefield V's Pacific expansion.

Its not the greatest campaign of all time, but it worked in creating fun scenarios to shoot through and I cared just enough to see it to the end and how it wrapped up. Honestly, its vastly superior to BF4's, as that game's story can literally put me to sleep. Unlike BF3, there is no former SAS operator to help create scenarios and redefine the dialogue and characters with lived-experiences, but that doesn't make the story pure slop either. 

I will say though, Subway-missions (specifically New York's) are becoming milslop's sewer levels, at this rate.

Pick it up if you can afford it and get a few good dozen or so hours out of it every few months.

[LAG] [ANTI-CHEAT] [SERWERY] [NETCODE] [CHEATERZY]

Schowałem się za osłoną, powiedziałem sobie „jestem bezpieczny" — sekundę później nie żyłem. Schowałem się znowu — i znowu zginąłem. Nie ginam według zasad gry, tylko według widzimisię serwera.

📶 OPÓŹNIENIA SERWERA

Stabilne połączenie, żadna inna gra nie laguje tak jak BF6. Nieraz dostałem obrażenia 1-2 sekundy po tym, jak schowałem się za ścianą. Netcode jest tak zepsuty, że strzelanie pierwsze, krycie się czy dobre ustawienie — nic nie ma znaczenia. Serwer po prostu mówi „nie, i tak już byłeś martwy" i cię zabija.

⚠️ ANTI-CHEAT: PRAKTYCZNIE NIE ISTNIEJE

Podobno jest anti-cheat. Świetnie. Więc dlaczego nadal obrywa się przez ściany, przez pojazdy, a czołgi lockują się na cel jakby miały aim-bota? Cheaterzy wciąż swobodnie chodzą po mapach. Ale najlepsze jest co innego: system blokuje legalne programy jak NVIDIA ShadowPlay, a nie oprogramowanie do cheatowania. Czyli nagrywanie klipów przez uczciwych graczy to problem, a cheaty — nie.

💀 TO NIE SĄ ANIMACJE ŚMIERCI, TO KOMUNIKATY SERWERA

Każda śmierć nie oznacza „byłeś w złym miejscu o złym czasie", tylko „serwer zaktualizował cię z opóźnieniem". Przeciwnik strzelił do ciebie, gdy ty już biegłeś gdzie indziej — ale dla serwera stałeś w miejscu sprzed dwóch sekund. To nie jest doświadczenie z grą, to wyścig pingów.

🛠️ WYDAJNOŚĆ

Po ostatniej aktualizacji zaczęły się zawieszenia. Mocny komputer, żadna inna gra nie ma problemów — ale BF6 potrafi zamrozić się w środku meczu. Sam anti-cheat obciąża system: urządzenia USB losowo się rozłączają, a gra czasem wyrzuca bez żadnego powodu.

Podsumowanie: graficznie imponujące, mapy ładne, potencjał jest. Ale gdy fundamenty techniczne są tak zepsute, nic innego nie ma znaczenia. Płacisz pełną cenę za produkt w stanie alfa. Nie kupujcie, dopóki EA tego nie naprawi.
