I've played all of the Battlefield games. In my opinion this is the worst, it's as if they took a superficial look at Battlefield 3&4 and tried to copy them without understanding what made them good games.

1. The gunplay and combat is awful, the guns themselves sound and feel weak. The time to kill is way too long and the time to die is too short. The recoil is a randomised spread rather than a controllable predictable pattern. Weapon and gadget variety is incredibly limited and the creativity possible in BF3&4 just isn't an option in BF6. The assault class in particular feels useless, without access to c4 you cant do anything against the over-armoured vehicles.
2. The maps are anti fun, lack balance, flow, and interesting topography. If you like to move and capture points good luck, the endless corners, windows and high ground camping spots will see you sniped before you can make it a few meters. 
3. No hardcore mode. Hardcore mode was incredibly popular in bf4, it still is today. For some unknown reason hardcore mode has been relegated to a custom game mode hidden in the server browser completely destroying the player count. Personally, i don't want to empty half a mag into someone to kill them and hardcore mode always felt more balanced than the vanilla options, its frustrating and disappointing to see it killed off when there is clearly still an audience for it.
4. Aggressive monetization. It is abundantly clear that this game was designed for monetiztion purposes first and gameplay 2nd. As soon as you boot the game up it cant wait to shove a battlepass rammed full of ridiculous cosmetics down your throat. It makes you wonder what the game might have been like if they directed the resources invested into designing hideous skins into making a better experience. It used to be that if a game sold well and earned a good player base that an expansion pack might be released, now they just try to nickel and dime you from the get go without earning the respect of their customers first.

This is not the Battlefield you are looking for.

I've never felt like I was playing mid-2010s Call of Duty more than I do when playing this game, in the worst possible way.

1. GUNPLAY & META PROMINENCE:
The hit registration, net code, and overall inconsistencies/imbalance in firearms results in an unrewarding gunplay that punishes creativity in playstyle in favor of a more modern, meta-focused gameplay style. Even if DICE/EA managed to fix their networking issues, the game would be trapped in a meta-prominent environment thanks to the introduction of movement tech and a huge disparity between best-in-slot and worst-in-slot weapons. The combination of fast-paced movement that makes targets harder to hit, bloom that makes targets harder to hit, and poor hit registration and networking issues that makes targets harder to hit, creates an environment where the easiest way to perform well is to choose high fire-rate weapons with low recoil. When one playstyle is drastically easier/better than any other playstyle, that's when you've developed a dooming meta that frustrates players and discourages them from playing in a way that they want. THIS IS THE PRIMARY REASON I'VE STOPPED PLAYING. As someone who likes to 100% all of the weapons, I've learned that a lot of the guns in the game are just unable to compete completely, even in the ranges they're supposed to succeed at. I'm done, trying.

DEVELOPER COMMUNITY INTERACTION:
The developers seem really in touch with the wrong parts of the community, and completely out of touch with the rest of it. They've tried for months to appease to helicopter and armor players, and it's going to do nothing good for the community in the end. They've entirely ignored requests to balance weapons, and the same 4 or 5 firearms in the game have comfortably resided in the meta since day 1. On top of that, they're doing the same thing that COD has been doing for years by introducing CRAZY OP guns every season, and then nerfing them by the time non-P2W players actually earn them. They continue to waste developer resources prioritizing the creation of micro-transactions and content for REDSEC that most players will never have the desire to experience.

Часто помітно гравців з інших франшиз, таких як Call of Duty, коли вони беруть медика і при цьому зовсім не розуміють своєї ролі в командній грі. Через це вони часто отримують негативні коментарі, а потім ідуть писати погані огляди, звинувачуючи гру. Але ком’юніті Battlefield дуже терпляче — воно пережило багато невдач від розробників. Після випуску дорожньої карти 2025 року, навпаки, стало видно, що розробники чують своїх гравців, розуміють їхні побажання і готові над цим працювати.

Я особисто безмежно радий оновленням і з нетерпінням чекаю нові сезони.

Battlefield — це поки що єдина онлайн-гра за останні 10 років, у якій я бачив, як люди дякують одне одному за гарний матч. Це багато говорить про спільноту.

Гру однозначно рекомендую всім фанатам якісного шутера, командної гри та просто гарного проведення часу.

Battlefield is the best game series that has existed, still exists, and, I’m sure, will continue to exist.

I’ve been playing Battlefield since Battlefield 3, spent over 500 hours in this franchise, and I can confidently say that Battlefield 6 is still played by the same loyal players who have been here for years.

You can often notice players coming from other franchises, such as Call of Duty, when they pick the medic class and have absolutely no understanding of their role in a team-based game. Because of this, they often receive negative comments and then go on to leave bad reviews, blaming the game itself. It’s hard to watch hype-chasers and random CoD players jump into Battlefield, play for a month, and then start hating on the game.

But the Battlefield community is very patient — it has survived many disappointments from the developers. After the release of the 2025 roadmap, it became clear that the developers are listening to their players, understanding what the community wants, and are willing to work on it.

Personally, I’m extremely happy with the updates and I’m genuinely looking forward to the new seasons.

Battlefield is still the only online game in the last 10 years where I’ve seen people thanking each other for a good match. That says a lot about the community.

I would like to thank DICE, Criterion, Ripple Effect, and Motive for their great work. And a special huge thanks for the ability to attach C4 to a drone and recreate the highly effective work of Ukrainian soldiers and drone operators in the game — that is truly a special detail.

Don’t listen to the haters — listen to the real fans of this game. They are the ones who carried their love for this franchise through the years and are ready to keep waiting as long as necessary.

I highly recommend this game to everyone who loves quality shooters, teamwork, and simply having a great time.

Much respect and love to both the developers and the fans.

I enjoy this game a lot, much more than BF 2042. Since launch, updates have improved the pacing for unlocking guns, attachments, and gear. The gameplay feels smooth and snappy, and the mechanics hold up well. The TTK can be frustrating, often soft-forcing you into specific meta builds to compete, but it remains a fun experience for 1-3 hour sessions. Hardcore servers can be a lot of fun for trying out less powerful or competitive weapons and slower paced gameplay, too. 

Unfortunately, the game is far from finished, which is par for the course with modern AAA titles. Season 2 added two new maps that are very fun, but some "new" content feels recycled from BF 2042. These assets should have been in the base game to begin with. The dev team seems to listen to player feedback, evidenced by their updated roadmap, though only time will tell if they deliver.

The aesthetic works well for a modern warfare setting. Most cosmetic skins are grounded, though the shop sells some goofy airsoft-style outfits that you rarely see others wearing. You can unlock a good amount of cosmetics just by playing, plus the battle pass system offers decent value at $10. It's a fair deal since you can earn in-game currency through the current pass to buy the next one. Although, I miss the days where you got all the content when purchasing a game or $10-15 full-fledged DLCs to add content instead of the live service model. Unfortunately for most games, those days have passed.

The gameplay leans closer to Call of Duty in its movement and gunplay, but it retains enough of the large-scale chaos to still feel like Battlefield.

At its current state, I rate it a 7.5/10. If the developers follow through on their proposed updates, that score will go up.

I recommend this game if you love the franchise, but if you are expecting the specific feel of Battlefield 3 or 4, you may be disappointed.

Finalizei a campanha de BF6 alternando com algumas partidas no multiplayer — e a sensação geral é clara: a franquia voltou com força.

A campanha é surpreendentemente sólida. A narrativa consegue te prender do começo ao fim, com um ritmo bem equilibrado entre ação intensa e momentos mais calmos que ajudam a construir os personagens. Aliás, os personagens são um dos pontos altos: bem escritos, carismáticos e com motivações convincentes, o que dá peso real às missões. Não é só sair atirando — você se importa com o que está acontecendo.

Tecnicamente, o jogo também impressiona bastante. O design de som é absurdo: tiros têm impacto, explosões são pesadas e o ambiente reage de forma convincente, aumentando muito a imersão. A dublagem está muito bem feita, com atuações naturais que ajudam ainda mais na construção da narrativa — nada soa artificial ou fora de tom.

A movimentação é outro destaque. Está fluida, responsiva e refinada. Tudo — desde correr, deslizar, mirar e trocar de posição — parece bem calibrado. Isso faz uma diferença enorme tanto na campanha quanto no multiplayer, porque o jogo responde exatamente como você espera.

Falando do multiplayer: ele está frenético, dinâmico e muito divertido. A sensação de caos organizado clássica da franquia está de volta. Os mapas favorecem combates intensos, e o gunplay é satisfatório do começo ao fim. Existem bots em algumas partidas, mas sinceramente não chegam a prejudicar a experiência — ajudam até a manter o ritmo em certos momentos.

Como alguém que jogou muito BF4, BF1 e BFV, dá pra dizer sem dúvida: esse jogo resgata o espírito da franquia. Ele pega o que funcionava nesses títulos e moderniza, sem perder a identidade. A imersão, o som, a movimentação e o ritmo das partidas mostram um cuidado que fazia falta.

No geral, BF6 entrega exatamente o que um fã esperava — e talvez até mais. É aquele tipo de jogo que te faz querer jogar “só mais uma partida” várias vezes seguidas.

Overall Impression
Battlefield 6 is a good game at its core, but it currently feels unfinished and requires significant patching. I recommend picking it up, but ideally during a sale.

Technical Issues & Latency
The biggest hurdle right now is latency. You will frequently experience getting shot through walls; while it might look like cheating, it’s actually a "desync" issue where your position on the server doesn't match what you see on your monitor. Furthermore, the DLSS implementation is inconsistent. In one session I can hit 150–170 FPS, only to see it drop to 110–130 FPS in the next, even on the same map and settings.

Content & Gameplay

Maps: The current rotation is lackluster. We need more variety and better map design to keep the gameplay fresh.

Singleplayer: The campaign is unfortunately way too short and feels underdeveloped. It had potential but ended just as it got started.

Player Count: Be aware that matchmaking can feel slow during late-night hours. If you play during the day, finding a full lobby isn't an issue.

Verdict: Buy it on discount. It’s playable and fun, but it needs work to reach its full potential.

They haven't learned a single thing from previous Battlefield titles. Vehicles completely break the game balance: you can easily rack up 10 kills in a single pass with an aircraft. To make matters worse, you only need to fly away for 30 seconds for your bombs to reload before coming back for another massive strike on a flag. Ground vehicles, instead of leading the charge, are being used as snipers, just like in 2042.

Players get to a flag and basically build a fortress in every single corner of the room. If you’re thinking of going in, think twice, because you’ll have four people watching every entrance, and all you’re going to achieve is getting yourself and your entire squad killed. Some maps are miles long, while others seem designed just to provide a constant dopamine hit of explosions, gunfire, footsteps, and people screaming. Bottom line: you have no idea what’s going on, and you die the moment you walk through a door because an enemy was camping in a corner (he’d been sitting there for five minutes just waiting for someone to pass by).

In some maps, like Manhattan, there are so many rooms, vertical levels, and rooftops that you never know where you're being shot from or where the enemies are. And if you’re playing on the Hagental Base map, you’re basically condemned to spend half the match running into a wall because, unlike the maps we had in 2042 or BF4, there is ONLY ONE HALLWAY. There’s no way to flank or try to take the flag behind the choke point; it’s incredibly frustrating. The maps and the game in general are so aggravating that the developers have had to resort to nostalgia once again, claiming they’ll bring back classic BF3 and BF4 maps—maps that actually worked and didn't suffer from a total lack of imagination like the current ones.

The game feels alright if you’re only interested in infantry-only modes. It’s a bit soul-crushing at first because your starting weapons won't kill anyone even if you catch them from behind, but that gets sorted out once you get attachments and unlock better guns. If you’re planning on playing modes like Conquest or anything involving vehicles, save yourself the trouble; it’s an even worse experience than what we had with BF2042. The only thing they’ve actually improved is that aircraft now go down in one or two missiles, and ground vehicles can be destroyed if you hit them from behind (unlike in BF2042, where it was practically impossible to kill them). The players are "toxic": you’ll always find them camping in a corner, prone on the floor, or sitting in an AA gun waiting for the chance to kill anyone just trying to get from one flag to another.

Also, there are times when you're in a gunfight and you duck behind a crate, wall, or door, yet you still die as if you never took cover. It would be great if they added a replay mode so we could see if there's a massive desync between what you see and what the server sees, or if some players just happen to have 'special powers' (cheats).

CONCLUSION:
The developers have really messed up by failing to fix the issues from previous Battlefield games and selling this title as if everything was fine and they’d actually listened to the community. Overall, the game is better, but it’s nowhere near the BF3 or BF4 experience they’re trying to sell us. If you can find it on a really good sale or at a shop for under $30-$40, you might want to consider it.

First and foremost, a massive shoutout and RIP to Vince Zampella – his genius is a massive contribution to what makes Battlefield 6 such a solid shooter, and why the community will be talking about the game for years to come.

Battlefield 6 is EA’s greatest gamble in years – a massive agglomeration of different studios working nonstop to make this game come to life. Did it pay off?

[h2] Campaign [/h2] 

Anyone familiar with the casual FPS scene would immediately understand what was the objective here – a narrative compelling enough to compete with CoD’s Modern Warfare story, adding the unique Battlefield twist to it. Sadly, 6 was, once again, not the one to compete head-on with CoD on this front.

The story itself is… okay? Pax Armata appear strong enough and real enough that such situation could almost feel like a potential scenario in our own world. The story, while kinda bland at certain points, could be passable enough for the most it, and it actually includes some very cool scenes such as the Gibraltar landings, the Manhattan chases, and [spoiler] the all-out, massive base attack [/spoiler] at the end of the game.

Yet – something is missing. In the constant chase of CoD’s formula, Battlefield forgot to create their own. The characters, while interesting at times, fail to create engagement on the level of Blackburn, Dima, Pac or Irish from previous entries. I quite liked Murphy – but I felt his character wasn’t explored as it should be. Hemlock, man… you are not Ghost.

You can try it once and see for yourself. Trust me – one time is enough.

[h2] Multiplayer [/h2] 

This is Battlefield’s bread and butter – and it shines very much here. 

There’s a reason why the game was the #1 sold game of 2026. While it has its faults, the shooting, the chaos, the explosions, the audio, the level of detail – everything comes to life when you jump into a lobby and start blasting away. 

Every lobby has its own rivalries, every game you get the chance of writing a new moment to tell for ages. An objective defense with an LMG firing nonstop. A tank battle where you have one eye on target, and one eye in your tank’s health. A well placed RPG splitting that darn helicopter in two. The sweet, sweet sneaky takedown to steal that camper’s dogtags. Every game - a new challenge.

Gunplay wise, the game feels quite amazing. Guns and gadgets have their adaptability to certain scenarios and engagements, and you will 100% certainly find the right tool for your tastes and skill. The gun pool increases every passing season, so new fresh options are constantly showing up.

Yeah yeah, sure – there are issues with it since day one. Small maps, a Portal mode that was gutted, netcode issues… The list can go on. Some of them are indeed in need of being fixed (at the moment I’m writing this, most of them have), others are just grievances of a community who just wants every single entry to be Battlefield 4 Remaster and nothing else.

[h2] Final Thoughts (Season 1 and after) [/h2] 

As the Seasons have started to come and go, and with the 2026 Roadmap being announced, it’s clear that Battlefield 6 is setting the stage to be one of the most remarkable entries in the saga. Battlefield Studios have tried (so far) to listen to the community and try to deliver on making this one of the best shooters in recent years.

Only time will tell. As of now, however, I’ve been having great fun with the game.
In your case, whether casual or hardcore, vehicle or infantry main, Medic or Recon – I’m sure you will have fun too.

I honestly don’t know what happened to Battlefield 6, but this is easily the worst Battlefield experience I’ve had.

The maps are incredibly boring and poorly designed. They’re full of random clutter and angles that heavily favor campers, making aggressive or tactical play feel pointless. Instead of rewarding movement and positioning, the game basically encourages people to sit in one spot and wait.

Vehicle balance is also a mess. Anti-tank weapons feel ridiculously weak — it takes far too much effort to deal with vehicles, which completely ruins the infantry vs. vehicle dynamic that Battlefield used to do so well.

The weapon design is another big disappointment. Most guns feel the same, with very little identity or uniqueness. It’s like the only thing that matters is rate of fire — everything else is irrelevant. There’s no personality, no memorable weapons, just copy-paste variations.

Overall, this is the worst Battlefield game I’ve ever played. Massive step backward.

作为一名战地爱好者，在游戏发售伊始，我就毫不犹豫地预购了《战地风云6》标准版。但数百个小时体验下来，我的感受相当复杂。总的来说，这一部作品给我的感觉可以用“巨人回归，但步履蹒跚”来形容。作为大战场游戏最严厉的父亲，战地新作无疑仍是这一体裁中的巨人；不过只要是认真游玩该作的玩家都会明白，这位巨人尽管身形依旧伟岸，但已经步履蹒跚、垂垂老矣，浑身弥漫着一股无可救药的恶臭。

当初从A测到B测的游玩体验，仿佛让我看到了dice工作室的诚意，至少他们是在认真做游戏的。不过第一赛季的正式开始就略微打破了我的美好幻想，其中最为人诟病的便是极其迷惑的枪械配件解锁进度，慢得简直令人望而生畏：一些基础配件的解锁需要玩家在苛刻条件下反复堆积击杀数，用着手感操作极差的裸枪，一遍遍重复着麻木的操作。这种“上班式”的解锁进度导致大量玩家在前中期几乎无法享受武器配装的乐趣。虽然制作人在随后的一次访谈中承认了这确实是“发布初期的失误”，并在后续补丁中尝试调整了挑战系统，但早期体验的钝痛感已经深深地烙印在了那一批玩家的记忆里挥之不去。

同时，我们应当注意到，今天的dice已经失去了制作优质战地地图的能力，这一点在首发地图上尤为明显。首发地图普遍偏小，缺乏传统《战地》应有的开阔战场纵深，反而呈现出类似 COD 的紧凑巷战格局。对于期待在战场多维度中畅游载具、步步为营推进战线的老玩家而言，这种设计无异于一盆冷水。而且以我的个人体验为例，在突破模式中，除了开罗围城之余的其他地图设计堪称糟糕，甚至毫无设计感可言，让我不禁怀疑是否是交由AI制作的。米拉克山谷、解放峰等所谓大地图，从进攻方到防守方总部一以贯之，丝毫没有大战场该有的纵深、平衡性以及趣味性不说，还充斥着各种意义不明的载具反斜、打狙圣地、无掩体裸奔空地，简直是糟糕透顶。这一切不禁想让我问一句，大战场的气息在哪里？

况且，作为现代战争而言，主战坦克几乎丧失了全部战场威慑力，几枚火箭弹就能轻松将其化为废铁。步兵单位对重型载具的压制能力过强，导致本作的主战已然成为移动棺材。作为铁皮玩家，最大的感受是深深的无助感。再加上大多数突破模式空载的缺席，标志着载具系统的严重失衡。

最有趣的是，战地6的赛季更新堪称dice给玩家上的免费PUA课：赛季间隔几个月，新图大概率就两张。对于一款21世纪的大作，这般持续运营的感人效率也就dice做的出来。如此产能低下，以致于每次更新都会出现bug然后拖着不修直到下次大规模更新又出现了新的bug便不奇怪了吧？不过既然已经低到这种程度，你们怎么就忘不了你们的勾史大逃杀？dice要不要去玩家社区里看看有几个人愿意玩你们的大逃杀，又有几人在意？

有一说一，战地6的优化水准确实在线，开发商主动放弃光追死磕高帧率，确实值得某些厂家学三年。然而当我看到某些重制后的老图在空气中散发AI生成的生硬感，刚想夸的口又咽回去了。把经典图炒冷饭都充斥着一股子SD生图和风格化滤镜的诡异感。这是致敬经典还是暴打情怀？dice如果能开窍回到当年BF1的审美巅峰，现在的日活也不至于从首发七十万流失近倍。

总而言之，EA再用这套先透支情怀后画大饼补丁缝补半年的运营哲学试探玩家，可能下一部——不，不会再有下一部了。高压的对局环境、离奇的ttk、糟糕的地图滤镜、平衡性缺失的地图设计以及其他很多我没来得及提到的问题……这一部跟完不完美不搭边，只能说至少能玩。

看在我玩了几百个小时的份上，我还是给个推荐吧。

This is Battlefield at its absolute peak.

Battlefield 6 doesn’t just return to form it kicks the door off its hinges and reminds everyone why this franchise dominated the genre in the first place.

I’ve been playing Battlefield since Battlefield 2: Modern Combat (2005), so I don’t say this lightly this feels like the series firing on all cylinders again. 

Honestly, it would be amazing to see some kind of in-game “veteran” recognition system added, something that highlights players who’ve been with the franchise through the years. A small badge, tag, or stat tracker would be a really nice touch and a cool way to honour long-time players.

The scale is insane. Massive maps, all-out warfare, vehicles tearing across land, air and sea - soon?
it’s pure chaos, but the kind of chaos that feels controlled and intentional. Every match turns into its own cinematic moment without feeling scripted.

The gunplay is tight, responsive, and genuinely satisfying. Whether you’re in close-quarters fights or picking people off at range, everything just feels right. 
Pair that with the destruction system, and no two engagements ever play out the same. Buildings crumble, cover disappears, and you’re constantly forced to adapt.

And then there are those classic “only in Battlefield” moments jets screaming overhead while tanks push objectives, squads working together, absolute madness unfolding in every direction. It’s the kind of experience no other shooter really delivers at this scale.

Playing with friends takes it to another level. Proper squad play actually matters again, and when it clicks, it really clicks.

Visually, the game looks incredible. The lighting, the environments, the atmosphere it all adds to that immersive, boots-on-the-ground feel.

That said as a long-time fan, I do think part of Battlefield’s dip over the years came from what I’d call the “codification” of Battlefield leaning too hard into trends like battle royale. Modes like “REDSEC” never really felt like Battlefield at its core. Even the naming felt off if you’re going to do it, why not just call it Battlefield Royale and own it?

But here’s the thing, Battlefield 6 feels like a course correction. A proper return to identity.

Let’s hope the BF 2026 roadmap keeps that momentum going and pushes the franchise back to the forefront where it belongs.

It genuinely feels like the devs finally understood what makes Battlefield… Battlefield.

No gimmicks. No nonsense. Just all-out war done right.

Anyway, that’s enough talking.

Buy it. Deploy. Enjoy the chaos.

Questa non vuole essere una recensione del titolo, prendetela più per uno sfogo "sfogo" da consumatore affezionato alla saga e che si sente preso in giro per l’ennesima volta dopo aver speso 100€. 
Ci avevo sperato tanto e avevo creduto che questo nuovo gioco sarebbe stato diverso. Ho comprato tutti i titoli della saga a partire da BC2 e mi ci sono divertito sempre e comunque ma purtroppo, ho visto un mio personale declino nel riuscire a mandare giù tante cose dei nuovi capitoli.
Il capitombolo fatto da FB5 era stato un primo campanello di allarme ma “poteva starci” essendo l’unico capitolo che non mi entusiasmò rispetto a tutti quelli giocati in precedenza, la piega che aveva preso il 2042 più simile ad un hero shooter e gli innegabili problemi problemi tecnici che abbiamo riscontrato tutti mi hanno fatto abbandonare il titolo dopo un centinaio di ore, sebbene la cosa non mi fosse andata troppo a genio poteva ancora “starci” se guardato come un tentativo di svecchiare il titolo da meccaniche un po’ trite (ma sempre apprezzate) dei giochi precedenti.
All'annuncio di BF6 ci sono andato con i piedi di piombo guardando i contenuti pubblicati da svariati content creator, ho aspettato il lancio per informarmi su recensioni, impressioni a caldo e a freddo e dati gli elogi ricevuto nonostante la titubanza all’acquisto, dopo un paio di settimane BF6 era nella mia libreria. 
Il gioco mi aveva preso, la campagna alla fine si sapeva già di partenza che sarebbe stata relativamente una monnezza e che alla fine puntavamo tutti per il comparto PvP. Il gioco mi ha divertito un sacco all’inizio, e mi aveva fatto ritrovare il divertimento del giocare la sera dopo il lavoro, le premesse e i "mea culpa" da parte di DICE ed EA sembravano effettivamente sincere e che forse avremmo visto un signor gioco dopo 2 capitoli non proprio all’altezza.
Ero così preso bene che ho persino comprato il pacchetto PRO per la prima stagione. Ma dopo 180 ore di gioco, dopo aver assistito a promesse non mantenute, a contenuti inesistenti (nonostante lo shop fosse sempre bello aggiornato di adesivi inutili, ciondolini e skin vendute a peso d’oro), sever che non reggono le partite, sessioni pilotate da sistemi di SBMM, e tante altre belle cose che leggerete in recensioni migliori della mia.. dopo più di 15 anni e soldi spesi su questa saga.. non comprerò mai più un capitolo di BF.

Premiera i pierwsze wrażenia były całkiem dobre - wiadomo było trochę niedociągnięć i oczekiwań co przyniosą następne aktualizacje. 

Po pół roku od premiery stwierdzam, że z deklaracji za dużo nie wynikło. Najlepszy przykład - netcode - dalej jest problem z otrzymywaniem DMG już w ukryciu. Od jakiegoś czasu jest też problem z freezowaniem PC na procesorach X3D przez anticheata. Społeczność rozwiązała ten problem - wystarczy włączyć igpu ale łatki dalej nie ma. Osobiście nie mogę grać więcej niż 15 minut. 

To samo dotyczy np. balansu broni - balistyka leży.  Gra wymusiła mapami walkę na bliskim dystansie ale bronie jakoś tego nie odzwierciedlają. Mam wrażenie, że  nie ma większych różnic między kalibrami, waga - po prostu statystyki. Najlepiej to widać jak np. na dystansie 70 m strzelamy do snajpera z np. PW5A3. Jak nie trafi nas w głowę to szybciej zasypiemy go gradem pocisków po 20 dmg niż on przeładuje xD Dla mnie aktualny balans broni nie istnieje - po prostu bierz co szybko i stabilnie strzela. Dlatego gra ma spore problemy z meta bulidami broni. O pojazdach można by było podobną epopeje napisać. 

O mapach można powiedzieć to samo - od premiery gracze chcą większych map, a w kółko dostajemy małe i mniej niż byśmy chcieli. 

Jedyne czym dla mnie broni się BF to klimat - faktycznie czuć, że to pole bitwy i bardziej mnie wciąga niż V czy 2042. Jedynie jakbym miał się czegoś uczepić to kreacji frakcji PAX - tak wiem, polityka i te sprawy. Wolałbym coś bardziej ukierunkowanego niż jacyś nijacy najemnicy. 

Czy warto kupować? Nie wiem, narzekam ale zagram z dwa mecze. Zauważyłem, że mniej osób gra i są problemy z matchmakingiem i niezbalansowanymi drużynami. Ostatnio jeden mecz na przełamaniu skończył się po 4 minutach. Raczej efekt tego, że zostali gracze, którzy w to ciągle grają. Daje negatywa bo zakładam, że w 2027 powoli zaczną wygaszać tytuł, a wątpię, że dużo się zmieni do tego czasu. Kto kupił ten kupił.

Literalmente iniciaron una Open Beta para traer de vuelta toda la playerbase veterana, y una vez que salio el juego, empezaron a meterle updates/modificaciones más al estilo CoD (por obvias razones, plata), un ejemplo CLARISIMO de esto es que cualquier clase puede usar cualquier tipo de arma. Cosa que, si estabas vendiendo el juego como un "sucesor espiritual" de Battlefield 4, va totalmente en contra del objetivo o de lo que nos habian planteado desde un inicio.

Otro problema que lo considero enorme, ya que lo que estoy jugando es un BF y no un CoD, es que no parecen nerfear armas que estan un toque desbalanceadas, es decir, infligen un daño por encima de lo que deberian o tiene una cadencia de disparo altisima (lo que hace que el TTK este tmb desbalanceado). ¿Que sucede? Simple, todo el mundo se empieza a equipar estas armas (armas meta) y al final la partida se convierte en un Team Deathmatch, en vez de un Breakthrough, que vendria ser como el modo mas frecuentado. ¿Es culpa de la gente? En parte si pero no, digamos, si vas a jugar solo por matar y andar solo por ahi, ¿por que no te vas a jugar al CoD o al Fortnite? Y a la vez no, porque EA/DICE/Battlefield Studios/lo que sea es el que permite este tipo de mecanicas.

De la misma manera, no se respetan los roles de las clases y no parecen haber consecuencias por ello, por ejemplo, un medico que no revive, no cura (se cura solo a si mismo), no aguanta en los puntos, etc. o por ejemplo, gente que juega de ingeniero pero no destruyen ni un tanque/helicoptero o no reparan, un recon que no mata al sniper enemigo o ni marca enemigos, etc... Despues por ejemplo, por esto mismo se ven reviews negativas de que los vehiculos estan OP, en realidad, son OP porque nadie esta dispuesto a tirarlos abajo y al final uno es el unico bldo cambiando de clase para hacer lo que nadie hace.

Tema modo Portal y servidores custom, haria que la XP no se gane mediante esos medios, ya que veo mucha gente de nivel mayor a 100 y no saben ni el modo que estan jugando o que carajo es un push.

Para mencionar algunos puntos positivos:
- Los mapas estan buenos, y la destruccion esta bastante bien, diria como BF3/4.
- Los graficos y la ambientacion esta bien lograda.
- El tiempo en encontrar un enemigo es corto, cosa que siempre vas a andar a los tiros.
- El diseño de las armas, los controles y los disparos esta tambien bien logrado.

En fin, yo creo que si EA revierte la jugabilidad a como era en la Open Beta con el nerfeo del slide, que en la misma OB estaba medio roto, el juego estaria mucho más vivo o por lo menos, mas divertido de lo que esta actualmente. Espero que este año con el anuncio de los nuevos mapas y futuras actualizaciones vaya mejorando el panorama (cosa que no creo).

I booted up Battlefield 6 expecting a gritty, tactical war experience. What I got instead was cardio training, emotional damage, and a deep personal relationship with the respawn screen.

The graphics? Stunning. Truly. I’ve never seen such beautifully rendered explosions immediately before being deleted by someone using A Sniper from three postal codes away.

The gameplay is incredibly immersive. For example:

I spawned in.
I took two steps.
I died.
I reflected on my life choices.

Rinse and repeat. 10/10 realism.

The vehicles are also fantastic. I especially enjoy watching tanks from a distance, as they vaporize me before I can even finish saying “is that a—”.

Teamwork is key in this game. Unfortunately, my team consists of:

A guy flying a helicopter into a building
Someone blasting music through their mic
Me, crawling in the dirt like a confused NPC

Sound design deserves praise too. The distant gunfire, the roaring jets, and the very clear sound of my dignity leaving my body.

Would I recommend Battlefield 6?
Yes—if you enjoy chaos, cinematic deaths, and being humbled on a spiritual level.

Play it for the graphics.
Stay for the trauma.

             Сильная сторона игры — динамичные матчи. Бои проходят быстро, экшена много, почти всегда что-то происходит: взрывы, техника, перестрелки за точки, хаос и напряжённые моменты. Когда команда играет слаженно, игра действительно затягивает и напоминает, за что серию любят.
             Графика достойная: хорошие эффекты дыма, освещение, детализация оружия и техники. Звук тоже сильный — выстрелы, вертолёты, танки и взрывы создают нужную атмосферу войны.
             Но есть и спорные моменты. Часть игроков считает, что некоторым картам не хватает масштаба и ощущения большой войны. Карты более плотные и ориентированы на постоянный экшен, из-за чего меньше пространства для манёвров, дальних флангов и тактической игры техникой. Для одних это плюс, для других минус.
             После последних патчей разработчики исправили часть ошибок, улучшили баланс и добавили доработки, но проблемы полностью не ушли. Игроки всё ещё жалуются на:

* вылеты и нестабильность на PC
* просадки FPS после обновлений
* спорный hitreg
* редкие баги интерфейса
* периодические проблемы с подбором матчей
* отдельные вопросы к балансу оружия и техники

Short Review: 7.8/10

Long Review:
After 93 Hours (as of writing this review) I can safely say that this game is good but not 70$ good allow me to elaborate in the way I usually do, The Good, The Bad, The Ugly

The Good: 
Graphics and Performance look and feel great, but make no mistake this won't run on your grandma's potato you will need atleast a RTX 3060 minimum to run this game you could probably get past with a 1080ti but newer cards will perform better, the gunplay is solid, very responsive and nice feeling, movement is quick, but not too sweaty with CoD like movement so don't expect to see anyone slide cancelling or moving crazy. Some of the maps are really solid like the new Hagental Base which radiates heavy Operation Locker Vibes. Vehicle combat can be satisfying at times, and Support feels way more rewarding.

The Bad: 
Where do I start, some maps are absolutely chopped either in scale or with the layout, a solid example being Operation Firestorm (yes that one map from BF4) the scale is messed up entirely my guess is because they eyeballed photos of op firestorm when designing the BF6 remake instead of importing the game map from BF4 and remaking the new one over the old one, so it feels 10x smaller than the original did. Medics/Support also just seem to not do their jobs 90% of the time I'm guessing maybe because their new or just don't care but the amount of times I've seen Medics run past me while I'm downed and it's perfectly safe is disappointing. Lastly Vehicle Combat can be a bit annoying especially air combat, since majority of the maps currently are small or medium, jets don't work well on the maps, resulting in you getting obliterated after taking off, either from SPAAG across the map, or like 7 players with Stinger Missiles, ground combat can be frustrating as the meta is to hit weakspots resulting in some vehicles just being 1 shot.

The Ugly:
The Campaign sucks, which is kinda sad because the Voice Actors gave it their all, but they got done dirty by the horrid scriptwriting, the Campaign is also very short so it's not nearly as involved as past titles have been. The UI for the main menu is absolutely horrible, looking more similar to a streaming platform than a game, this is a common thing games have began doing specifically Triple A titles and it's infuriating because it just makes things more confusing as opposed to simplifying things. REDSEC is another massive painpoint, it's great, lots of fun don't get me wrong, but all those devs working on it could have worked on the campaign and it may have turned out better, instead we get a Battle Royale (dying genre) that's supposed to be a competitor to CoD's Warzone but falls short. Another problem with the game is the way they handle cosmetics and unlocks, they are strictly seasonal, including unlocks from challenges, some locked to "earlier in the season" meaning some items are just no longer unlockable, they need to atleast add a rotation in the shop or challenges so we have an opportunity to unlock old items again, and make challenges weekly not seasonal or monthly. And by far the biggest painpoint and ugliest aspect is the lack of a proper server browser with proper persistent servers and also the ability to self host servers (which would keep BF6 alive even after EA & DICE stops supporting the game).

All of these things being said and considered the game ranks 7.8/10, while the game has plenty pain points and isn't worth the full price, I would say it's worth it onsale, atleast half off if not less.

After a fantastic launch full of promise and momentum, BF6 has been left to stagnate and the gaps in its original gameplay are now gaping holes in its core loop as a combined arms game. 6 Months with a medley of maps, equipment, and gimmicky events have done nothing but widen the problems in gameplay. 

At the core, the problem is speed. BF6 is a fast game: faster than all previous titles. Faster TTK, faster TTD. Faster map load times, fast matches, fast matchmaking. Fast time to fight. The result is a game where there's little time to think, even less time to react -- and only one way to play: Fast. 

Compare this then with the speed of new content, development, and the reactivity of the game as a experience: Slow. Unlocks were slow (this was patched only recently), new weapons, events, and maps are slow to arrive. Battlepass is slow to unlock. New basic features were slow to arrive, if they arrived at all. HUD color accessibility? months after launch - and reticle color accessibility - months later even after that.

IG communication is nonexistent on most servers. There is no match-made VOIP. The servers themselves have no browser experiences that let communities gather and build consistently. Players are dropped unceremoniously between games and not allowed to team up or participate in anything meaningfully. Player group limits, low speed server performance, extremely long refresh rates and poor reactivity hamper the moment to moment gameplay. Not to mention the travesty that is Portal: even curated Portal experiences are janky, cumbersome messes that barely function properly. And even when they do, they are on the lowest refresh rate, making them exceptionally prone to rubberbanding and other performance issues that suck all the fun out of any creativity the designer might have intended. Acknowledging that the store has resisted adding a crazy skin, it has added so little of interest that it isn't worth the menu space. Even if there was a neat skin, the skin browser itself is a mess of deep menus of units and lore that absolutely nobody remembers--but players do quickly realize that the overpriced skin they purchased are faction AND class specific, meaning you are only able to enjoy it in half of your games anyway.

The combined arms aspect is the weakest it has ever been in Battlefield. Gone is any semblance of interaction between the various vehicle types on any map besides Conquest Large The ground vehicle gameplay leaves the most to be desired: when a single engineer has enough offensive strength to defeat any vehicles, those vehicles are forced to play cowardly and pathetically in order to survive. One of the first changes made to this game was to ensure that Engineers default kit spawns with enough rockets to solo any vehicle in the game. I believe this to have been the fundamental error made in the early weeks of this game to remove any semblance of meaningful vehicle combat. Combined with the variety of rocket devices, all of which are lethal in their own way, ground vehicles have exceptionally few ways to counterplay. Vehicles like the IFV and Armored Transports are the top vehicles because they can spawn infantry; infantry strength is king on all smaller maps. MBTs have it the worst and are often featured as the maps' prize vehicle but in nearly every situation it is outclassed by the IFV, except for fighting other MBTs. Infantry weapon balance is its own situationthat I personally haven't been willing to extensively participate in, but its the classic that all other FPS games struggle with. High ROF, low recoil dominate at every range except long. Midrange is filled with gimmicks like 1KO shotguns and sweet-spot DMRs, there's plenty to choose from if you like fast. The short TTK and TTD makes them all equally fun and frustrating to play with or against.

At the end here, I don't have faith that substantial changes to the game are on the way to bring this game back into the promise of its combined arms gameplay; the game has lacked a coherent vision from the start and I fear that at this point: the game is not brave enough to accept one.

Netcode, (des)balanceamento de matchmaking, (des)balanceamento de mapas, principalmente para o ataque nos modos de avanço (breakthrough, rush) e excesso de lobbies formados com bots são as maiores desgraças desse jogo.

Adicionarem um modo battle royale quando já existem vários do gênero, que está em declínio, também foi uma das decisões mais estúpidas já tomadas porque tiraram o foco do jogo principal, contribuindo para o declínio do BF6. Além disso, eles não separaram o BR do jogo base, o que significa que se você consultar a quantidade de players totais ativos na Steam não saberá quantos daqueles estão jogando o BR ou o jogo base, mascarando o real engajamento em cada um deles. Mas dada a dificuldade atual de formar lobbies com players, que tem sido em sua esmagadora maioria de bots, pode ser que o jogo base tenha muito menos players ativos do que os dados da Steam sugerem.

Ainda sobre a criação de lobbies, é importante pontuar que eles criaram um sistema imbecil de lobbies: eles criam múltiplos lobbies de um mesmo modo de jogo, quando o correto deveria ser juntar num único lobby todos os players que querem jogar aquele determinado modo e com o excedente de players, sim, criar um novo lobby. O resultado desse sistema imbecil são as inúmeras salas com bots que não são preenchidas com players e às vezes uma partida inteira se desenrola somente com bots porque eles fracionaram a base de players em diversos lobbies com bots.

Ainda tem a suspeita de EOMM como cereja do bolo, o que também influencia no matchmaking e nos lobbies.

O jogo começou bem, gosto da franquia e gosto muito do BF6, mas a cada dia que passa está ficando mais insuportável jogar esse jogo da desgraça pela imensa frustração que ele proporciona.

O que era fonte de diversão, agora se tornou uma grande fonte de frustração. Não à toa a queda imensa de players desde o lançamento.

Torço para que a EA acorde e tratem os problemas do jogo nas atualizações que virão, sendo o mais frustrante e preocupante atualmente o netcode. Mas dado o histórico dessa empresa desgraçada, não vou ficar sentado esperando.

Quando eu jogava o BF2042, eu dizia:

"Nossa, esse daqui, disparado, é o pior BF que eu já joguei..."

Quando houve o primeiro teaser do BF com Limp Bizkit, gerou um hype imenso em mim. Joguei a beta e, na época, o único problema que havia eram os mapas, que eram pequenos demais, e eu achava que no jogo base teríamos mapas maiores. No lançamento, os mapas continuaram pequenos para os padrões de Battlefield e, até o momento, não tem nenhum mapa grande nível Battlefield. Além de termos mapas pequenos, temos cenários onde veículos blindados usam e abusam de pontos específicos para ter uma visão ampla de todo o mapa. Se recebem dano de qualquer RPG, sempre tem algum engenheiro reparando o tanque; caso o veículo fique com pouca vida, ele apenas recua para um ponto onde o time adversário não tem visão e é reparado até ficar com a vida cheia.

Mas agora, falando do sistema de classes, é uma grande bagunça: todas as classes têm acesso a todas as armas. De início eu tinha esperança de que eles deixariam cada classe balanceada, mas não é o caso. É assim que funciona o propósito de cada classe agora:

Assalto: serve apenas para o Spawn Beacon.

Engenheiro: tem cinco RPGs e a ferramenta de reparo.

Médico: revive rápido e dá munição para o restante. Sobre a questão de o próprio pelotão conseguir reviver seus aliados, isso acaba tirando o propósito de ter médicos na partida. Afinal, se eu consigo reviver meus amigos sem estar com a classe de médico, não tem necessidade de utilizar esta classe para esse propósito, servindo apenas para dar munição.

Sniper: aqui se mantém o mesmo.

Com esse problema de não termos uma dinâmica real de classes e sem mapas que façam você ter a experiência do Battlefield clássico, depois de tantas horas de jogo posso dizer que eles adaptaram o frenesi de Call of Duty. Então, para finalizar: se você gosta da adrenalina que o CoD tem atualmente, este jogo é perfeito para você, pois não temos trabalho em equipe, a ideia é apenas matar os outros players e ignorar o objetivo.

Pelo amor ao seu dinheiro, não compre este jogo. Pegue apenas se estiver em uma boa promoção; de resto, apenas ignore.

If you're a BF fan you will find enjoyment somewhere between BFV and BF3. If you are not a BF fan and new to the franchise, you'll be blown away or hate it. As someone who isn't particularly anal about features in a game, this is probably the 3rd best BF game I've played personally. I've played every single one since BFBC2 and BF1 and BFV top this game. I'd prefer it over every other title. 

The only thing I really want from this game is proximity chat within 5-10m, specifically talking to vehicle crew not in your squad. Gunplay is A1. Visuals are A1, if your PC can handle it. Maps are a 7/10 (for me 9/10, but I'm trying to be reasonable), although, personally, I can enjoy every map given the teams are balanced and you don't get cornered. The maps will feel like hell for people who like to run and gun and not take it slow sometimes (in open areas). Most of the complaints I see are with performance, gameplay tactics that are unpopular (e.g. mortar/AA in team territory/strength of aircraft), and with the speed of updates. 

Regarding crashing, I think the game is stable, but PC owners can have so many different configs not to mention people messing with their own OS so take it with a grain of salt. My specs are attached and I play on high w/ some settings maxed above 100fps, no issues.

Almost every gameplay tactic 'issue' has a counter.. everyone is just too lazy to be the one to do it so they complain. Mortar in team territory can be solved with counter mortar. Non-Issue, and yes I'm the counter mortar. Oppressive Aircraft just needs AA on the ground (which no one likes to carry) to make them pop flares and a decent attack chopper pilot to finish them off with AA missile (aka team effort), or AA on ground to force pilots to fly low which renders them open to small arms/tanks/rpgs. AA in spawn... who cares? if you're the enemy, they literally leave capture points open to attack from the air, and if that's your teammate, they prevent spawn camping from enemy aircraft and provide a retreat area for friendly aircraft. Moot argument imo. As far as updates... its EA and none of you can develop games so there's two reasons right there you should just sit and wait. Back in my day we didn't even get updates and no info regarding what to look forward to was given LOL. Seriously though, I rather them take their time and make a sound update than release hot garbage. I think BF6 has another year of updates in it. Go play another game if you cant wait, so many out there!

It's a challenged game. EA has an extraordinary habit of ruining things that they get right. That being said, this game is a lot of fun.

My performance is smooth, the gunplay feels nice and I really love the addition of dragging to revive. The audio is perhaps the best in any battlefield game (save BF1) and I enjoy the setting (still think that Pax Armata looks like airsofters though).
Major problems in this game are definitely on the corporate side of things. We get 1-2 maps a season, with seasons being a whopping 3 MONTHS, we are still held hostage by constant monetization, the multiplayer content cycle is so slow that I have to grind weekly challenges and immediately swap games to save any sanity left, and the game is incomplete. There is no proper server browser, the maps are way too small and symmetrical, limited time modes take what could be an amazing concept and sets it to a monetized timeline, I could go on and on. 

TLDR;
This game has the bones to be one of the best entries in the franchise, coming from someone who's been on battlefield for a very long time. It has the systems intact to be incredibly unique, cinematic and fun, but those systems are ignored for a more traditional/shareholder-friendly marketing scheme. The devs listen and I appreciate that, but the problem truly lies in the EA side of things. I'm giving it a positive review because I believe in this game (especially with the recent roadmap, which looks great), and I do actually enjoy it. Lets hope that isn't broken.

I honestly don’t even know where to start. I thought hitting rock bottom with Battlefield 2042 was bad, but EA has somehow managed to drop even lower with Battlefield 6. It feels like they have completely forgotten what made this franchise great in the first place.

The gameplay experience is abysmal. The movement is clunky and unresponsive—it feels like you are constantly fighting the game mechanics just to traverse the map. It’s sluggish, heavy, and takes all the fun out of the pacing. When you finally get into an engagement, the gunfights are a total mess. They lack any kind of satisfying feedback, and the hit registration feels broken and inconsistent.

To make matters worse, the lighting is completely against you. I spend half my time getting killed by enemies I literally cannot see because they blend perfectly into the overly dark shadows or the poorly balanced environments. It feels like I’m playing a "guess where the bullet came from" simulator rather than a tactical shooter.

I am honestly just speechless and deeply disappointed in what EA has turned this series into. It’s a shell of its former self. I never thought I’d say this, but even Battlefield 2042 was a more enjoyable experience than this disaster. Save your time and money—this is a tragedy, not a Battlefield game.

Lost its direction — not recommended

This game had real potential during the beta, but since Season 2 it's completely lost and at this point, it’s not something patches are going to fix.

The biggest issue comes down to a clear design philosophy: “action around every corner.”
That approach has fundamentally hurt the game.

Instead of creating meaningful engagements, it results in:

Constant, chaotic firefights with no breathing room
No time or space to reposition, plan, or develop the fight
spawning directly in the line of fire.
Limited to nil ability to maintain a front. Constant 360 running around. 

It’s not that action is a problem — it’s that it’s been over-applied. Good gameplay needs contrast. Without slower moments, build-up, and positioning, the action becomes noise rather than something engaging.

Right now, the game plays like a weaker version of Call of Duty:

Extremely fast time-to-kill
Reaction-based gameplay over decision-making
Minimal reward for teamwork or tactical play

The usual response is “go play a milsim,” but that misses the point entirely. Players weren’t asking for full realism — they were expecting something in between.

There’s a clear spectrum:

Arcade shooters like Call of Duty or Counter-Strike
Full milsims on the other end
And games like Hell Let Loose that strike a more balanced, tactical middle ground

This game should have landed in that middle space. Instead, it’s leaned into constant chaos without the depth to support it.

Other ongoing issues:

Weapon mechanics: minimal recoil, little distinction between systems
Map design: generic layouts that reinforce constant engagement over flow
Update direction: focused on adding features rather than fixing core gameplay

On top of that, the player base has already taken a hit. Around six months post-release, server populations — particularly in regions like Australia — are thin enough to affect match quality.

At this stage, the direction is set. The core design philosophy is flawed, the gameplay hasn’t been corrected, and the player base is already declining.

Bottom Line

Not recommended. The “action around every corner” approach has stripped the game of depth, and it’s difficult to see any realistic path back.

It removes your ability to use positioning, flanking, or stealth because the other person already knows your next move. It’s not that you’ve lost your skill; it’s that the rules of the game have been broken. 
Those games from 2005–2014  (the BF2 through BF4 era) definitely felt different. While cheating existed, the community-rented servers with active live admins meant that a blatant cheater would usually get kicked and banned within minutes. Modern matchmaking often lacks that "neighborhood watch" feel, leaving players at the mercy of automated anti-cheat systems that can sometimes struggle to keep up.  

So do yourself a favor do not buy this game.

This post is to offset all of the blind hatred of the game while addressing some of the issues. 

I am a long time battlefield fan (BF 1942, BF 2, BF3, BF4, BF Hardline, BF1, BF5, BF 2042, and now BF 6

The Good:
BF6 is one of the most visually impressive and immersive FPS games that I have played outside of Milsims like Squad/Arma. The weapons feel reasonably distinct from one another, the attachment system is fun and makes you compromise on the what attachments you value most on your weapons. The classes feel truly meaningful even more so then in previous titles (I play with the weapons that historically were reserved to each class because I enjoy it). The team play opportunities are way better than previous titles with each class having a few very particular ways it can support the team. The maps are exceedingly detailed and tight with lots of kill zones and choke points to take advantage of. They are actively adding new maps including larger more traditional BF maps. Some of the good mechanics they added or improved upon:
- Dragging downed teammates (this is game changing and adds a tactical level to the game not present in previous titles)
- They brought back destruction even more detailed than before.
- They made every class serve a valuable purpose (Assault is meant to provide spawns, flanking, and objective capture advantages. Engineer specializes in taking out armor and defending friendly armor, Support provides smoke, cover, ammo, health. Recon provides overwatch, spots enemies for the team, and can even get away with laying traps and taking out unaware armor.)
- They added a few new game modes like Escalation, strikepoint, and some temporary modes that are fun and exciting, Not to mention the Portal mode which allows for custom game creation.

The BAD:
The bulk of the complaints that I have heard within the community seem to center around (EA Layoffs, Microtransactions, too COD like, Not enough content fast enough, the player base immediately dropped, etc.). 

Just like any game that has ever been made there are some things I would like to see changes or just not be present in the game. I agree with the community that some of the movements are a little too fast paced compared to previous titles (it is a military arcade style game after all not Squad/Arma). I'm not a fan of non-class locked weapons personally but for the most part people seem to be using weapons at least reasonably relative to their class. The non persistent servers aren't my favorite and can sometimes lead to longer times filling a match depending on time of day (but they are actively working to correct that). Aircraft can be powerful but they require a pretty high skill level to be effective with all the counters people have (toe guided missiles.... everywhere). I also personally don't think Redsec or Gauntlet ever needed to be in the game there are plenty of other titles that have it Battlefield is about the large scale conflicts or small team tactics on the defend/attack modes, But at the same time I never play it so who cares if its in the game. The Campaign, I really truly wanted to like it but I just couldn't. It felt like they tried the formula from BF3 with the nonsense of BF4 with less narrative for why any of it was even happening. The

My Devils Advocate:
Yes I get that people don't like microtransactions, yes I get people are angry that large chunks of the team was laid off, yes I get people are mad about the cosmetics. But who cares really? You don't have to buy the skins/battlepass to play the game (they are mostly stupid anyways). In terms of the layoff lets be honest with ourselves and see that this isn't exclusive to this industry every industry is facing major layoffs and difficulties.

While in some ways the complaints have merit, I think people fail to put a lot into perspective. For one games are just live service now, its not my favorite thing but its is what it is and we can thank streamer culture and games like COD and Fortnite for that. Before you would wait and pay for new maps and guns, now they slowly trickle in new content. 2-3 new maps and 4+ new guns every 12-18 weeks is pretty crazy in terms of content.

I think another big segment of the communities complaints focus on that the game isn't just a reskin of BF3 or BF4. I think that mindset is flawed personally because why would we pay for the same game again like seriously? I want games to grow and try new things like BF1, BF5, and BF6 did. BF6 is its own title building off what the Devs have learned through past titles.

Another major issue is with gamer culture itself constantly jumping from one game to the next and always needing more content y'all just can't seem to enjoy and make the most of what you have. Its only ever what we don't have that you talk about. People talk about the gaming being dead but it just isn't hell BF1 still has active servers and its player population is lower than 6's. The games population has remained stable over the last several months from when I have been periodically checking.

Additionally, Compared to many previous titles this is the most I have seen EA listen to the player feedback and genuinely try and improve the game. If you don't believe me look at the road map they dropped recently for the year (https://www.ea.com/en/games/battlefield/battlefield-6/seasons/battlefield-2026-roadmap).

If you made it this far I'm honored truly my goal with this wasn't to blindly worship at EAs alter but to try and give I think a fair and well thought out explanation of the current state of the game. I truly enjoy it and I am excited for the coming improvements like persistent servers and prox chat.

Developers are more focused on bloatware cosmetics than actual gameplay. Destruction is pitiful compared to BF4, and the new maps are few, boring, repetitive, and small.
Each update is up to 16GB of cosmetics for stuff you may not want to unlock or buy, but you still pay the price in hard drive space. Meanwhile, actual gameplay content suffers dramatically for it—all for a battle pass we weren’t even made aware of until weeks after release, complete with rampant FOMO and sunk-cost pressure since each season has been $25 or more.
The new maps feel very similar in style and flow, unlike in BF4 where most of the maps had these big dramatic destructive environments. You could completely change the flow of a game or battle by destroying a key building or zone. Flood Zone was one of my favorite maps because controlling the points wasn’t the only objective. Once you controlled more points, you could break the dam and flood the map, making mobility much more difficult and allowing your team to defend easier. But those tables could turn as well, keeping the game balanced.
Now the maps are fairly empty and already destroyed. Only small-scale destruction is available, and changing the course of a battle with one explosive is a thing of the past.
This was supposed to be Battlefield’s redemption, but it’s struggling to find players—so most games I join are half bots. I wish I could get a refund. Go back to Battlefield 4. It was the last good game from EA as far as I can see.

Jumping into Battlefield 6 is like strapping yourself to a rocket and lighting the fuse with a grin. The visuals are insane—smoke, debris, metal tearing apart, everything feels weighty and loud in the best possible way. Vehicles? Absolute beasts. Tanks rumble like thunder, jets scream overhead, and the battlefield feels alive with chaos.

This is war as a theme park ride. Infantry, cavalry-style vehicle pushes, air support raining down—just hop in, pull the trigger, and enjoy the ride. It’s the kind of game where you log on, cause some carnage, and log off with your ears still ringing.

But not everything lands clean.

The whole seasonal model? Yeah… not a fan. It starts to feel like a fashion show with guns. Skins, upgrades, “look how cool I am in the lobby guys”—and sometimes it edges a little too close to pay-to-win territory, or at least pay-to-flex. More toys, shinier gear, bigger advantage vibes.

Moment-to-moment gameplay though? Pure adrenaline. Dropping onto the battlefield in a tank, calling in support, radio humming in the background—it’s cinematic gold… right up until you’re instantly turned into scrap metal by a mine or an RPG hiding in a bush.

And that’s where the frustration kicks in.

Some weapons feel way too strong. RPGs deleting heavy armor like it’s made of cardboard? That stings. Especially when there are a lot of them. Tanks should feel like kings of the field, not expensive fireworks waiting to happen.

Then there are snipers… not the heroic recon type, but the lone-wolf mosquito squad. Sitting miles away, contributing nothing to the team, just picking people off and being endlessly annoying. You respect the aim, but not the vibe.

And weapon balance overall? It shouldn’t feel like a lottery ticket. Sure, an LMG should play differently than an assault rifle, and a shotgun should absolutely dominate up close—that’s the whole point. But within a class, the differences shouldn’t decide fights as much as they do now. Who cares which LMG you’re holding? The end result should be the same: plant your feet and rain bullets like a walking thunderstorm.

Still, the loop is simple and addictive: drop in, unleash chaos, get blown up, repeat. It doesn’t try to be your life—it just wants a slice of it.
And honestly? Sometimes that’s exactly what you want.

- La customización de las armas está bien. Si bien no es demasiado como su competencia directa (Delta Force), es más que suficiente para que la jugabilidad no sea monótona.

- Mapas chicos y medianos. Para algunas personas algo bueno, para otras (incluyéndome), falta de inmersión, sabiendo la grandeza que puede haber un Battlefield. Supongo que lo hicieron por el trauma que tuvieron con el 2042 en donde se fueron al otro extremo.

- El hitmaker/impacto de balas puede llegar a ser frustrante. No sé qué tiene con esta entrega que tienes que hacer muchos impactos de balas para matar un enemigo.

- Como todo BF, hay gente campera, full vehículos. Ni malo, ni bueno. Simplemente BF.

- Jugabilidad como del 2042, añadiendo más movimientos y mecánicas. Ta bien.

-Múltiple opciones gráficas, de sonido, interfaz, etc.

- Buenos detalles en la destrucción. Físicas normalitas. Gráficamente bueno.

- Por lo menos a mí me va bien de rendimiento (Adjunto mis specs)

- ¿Cumple con la premisa de volver a los viejos tiempos? Depende. Es una combinación entre un BF 3 ó 4 y 2042. Te puede sacar buenas horas de diversión. Y pensar que hace unos seis meses llegó a tener más de 700k, pero como todos sabemos, lo difícil no es llegar a esos números, sino mantenerlos.

BF 6 evokes a variety of emotions, but lately, it's been disappointing. It's not a lack of content (though I'm not picky about that), but something else entirely.
1: The problem is the community itself. The developers are making the game to meet community demands, yet the community itself refuses to play. I'm talking about the quality of the gameplay during the session itself, not about some inhumane reactions. The problem is that opponents pass each other, let you get to the rear, and then kill you in the back. Because of this, the modes: Conquest, Escalation, and Assault turn into chaos. I'm also amazed by people's desire to climb mountains and use sniper rifles. I don't understand why? They get shot down time after time, but they still climb up there. :))
2: The problem is the developer's stubbornness. Of course, there are probably some requirements imposed on the developer by managers "from above." But still, there are major issues that "break" the gameplay: a) Ads-Bloom b) Terrible registration, continuous desyncs. c) The ability to climb high mountains, or, more simply put, players are given the opportunity to occupy positions from which fire causes map imbalances. d) Map design – oh my god, some maps are simply unplayable. Just a solid field, 70% snipers – "play however you want." e) Sounds. There was an update after the New Year, after which the sounds were perfect, but after some updates, footsteps are unstable. Sometimes you can hear them, but most of the time you can't hear them.

As a result, we get a mediocre online experience, sometimes encountering bots on Sunday evenings.

And so on, there are a ton of other issues, but in my subjective opinion, what I've described is the bare minimum.

However, I admit the core of the game is very high-quality, but there haven't been any balancing changes that would significantly improve gameplay since September.

Compared to Battlefield 2, 3, and 4, this one feels like a major step down.

Why?

In standard multiplayer (not Battle Royale), the aircraft ceiling is far too low. The map boundaries leave almost no room to maneuver, so you end up an easy target for RPGs, tanks, and TOW missiles. With such tight map design, you’re often destroyed before you even have a chance to escape.

Weapon and attachment unlocks also feel painfully slow. There don’t seem to be any meaningful XP boosts like crates offering 2× XP for 24 hours or longer—at least none that are readily available—so progression ends up feeling like a grind.

Audio is another weak point. Using headphones with the game just doesn’t deliver the clarity or impact you’d expect.

Overall, matches feel more like chaotic bloodbaths than strategic battles. Survivability is extremely low, which takes away a lot of the tactical depth. In Battlefield 3, for example, maps like Metro allowed teams to actually hold positions with coordination, medics, and sustained firepower. And in Battlefield 4, larger maps like Caspian Border gave aircraft enough space to operate effectively without constantly being shut down.

Here, the tighter sandbox and design choices make the experience feel cramped, unbalanced, and ultimately frustrating.

Je suis un habitué de la licence Battlefield,  j’ai acheté tous les épisodes, mais honnêtement, ce 6ème opus est celui qui m’a le moins donné envie d’y jouer.

Le jeu possède pourtant de réelles qualités : de très beaux graphismes, des cartes réussies, une physique convaincante (notamment en ce qui concerne la destruction des décors), et le sound design très soigné.

Cependant, le principal problème vient, selon moi, du rythme de progression. On se retrouve très rapidement dépassé. Je suis un joueur qui aime progresser normalement, à son rythme (3h / 5h par jour). Malgré cela, j’ai l’impression de ne pas pouvoir faire évoluer mes armes assez vite par rapport à d’autres joueurs, qui utilisent des modes personnalisés sans véritables adversaires pour éliminer des bots en boucle pendant des heures.
Personnellement, je ne souhaite pas que ma progression se résume à ce type de méthode. Je veux simplement avancer de manière classique, en jouant normalement. Or, à cause de cet écart de progression, je me retrouve rapidement désavantagé, ce qui finit par nuire à mon expérience de jeu.

De plus, j’ai le sentiment que l’on fait assez vite le tour du contenu. Cela enlève une grande partie de la saveur du jeu, surtout lorsque l’on ajoute à cela l'énorme écart de progression expliqué récemment.

Concernant la campagne solo, je l’ai trouvée très décevante. L’histoire est, à mon sens, mal racontée, les personnages manquent cruellement d’intérêt, et l’intelligence artificielle est loin d’être convaincante. Je me suis tout de même forcé à aller jusqu'au bout, mais l’expérience ne m’a jamais réellement accroché. Pour être honnête, je me suis même ennuyé au point de m’endormir dessus.

Le mode Battle Royale ne m’a pas davantage convaincu. Il donne l’impression de reprendre une formule déjà vue du côté de Call of Duty, sans vraiment apporter quelque chose de neuf ou de mieux maîtrisé. Mes premières parties étaient agréables, mais l’intérêt retombe assez vite. Le mode semble peu évolutif et manque de mises à jour ou de nouveautés marquantes.

C’est d’autant plus frustrant que la bêta ouverte de Battlefield 6 m’avait énormément plu. J’y ai passé environ 30 heures, et même si son contenu était forcément limité, puisqu’il s’agissait d’une bêta, l’expérience me paraissait beaucoup plus équilibrée. Il n’y avait pas encore cet écart de progression causé par les modes personnalisés permettant de monter ses armes artificiellement en éliminant des bots pendant des heures.

En conclusion, je suis extrêmement déçu par Battlefield 6. À mes yeux, ce jeu avait un grand potentiel de relancer fortement la licence, mais certains choix de conception et de progression et de réalisation ont fini par gâcher une partie importante de l’expérience.

Battlefield 6.

Kde jen začít. Hned v úvodu...začal jsem hrát day one na PS5, aktuálně tam mám přes 130 hodin. Tady na PC mám 80 hodin, celkem tedy lehce přes 200 hodin. Především bude moje recenze mluvit k těm pokročilejším hráčům a k někomu kdo hledá multiplayer, ve kterém by chtěl utopit stovky hodin.

Začněme tím pozitivním...

Battlefield 6 se hraje skvěle. Movement zde prošel řádnou ''modernizací'' a lehce nám Battlefield ''CODkovatí'' . Je to špatně? Nemusí být. Svižnější movement, repsonsivnější ovládání tomu sedí a překvapivě se vám to celé dostane do ruky mnohem dříve než by jeden čekal. Audio stránka hry je opět na vysoké úrovni. Já bych sice stále zařadil na první místo Battlefield V, který je bitevním ozvučením téměř bezkonkureční, ale Battelfield 6 by se klidně dal zařadit mezi top 3 nejlépe ozvučených dílů ze série. Do pozitiv je potřeba zařadit i aktuální výběr režimů. Najdete zde stálice jako Conquest, Teamdeathmatch ale i velmi oblíbený nový režim Escalation a mnoho dalšího. Ani výběr zbraní neurazí a nabízí širokou škálu druhů zbraní, attachmentů a vylepšení. 

Z pozitivní noty bych teď přešel do mírně negativnější, nicméně i tady se otřeme o kladné stránky hry...

Battlefield 6 je bezesporu ten díl s největším potenciálem. Kdo tvrdí opak, je hlupák. Prostě to tak je. Na druhou stranu je nutné dodat, že tento potenciál se studiu ani zdaleka nedaří naplnit. Topí se ve vlastních chybách, popírají sami sebe, nedoručují co bylo slíbeno apod. Jako by si tady i samotné EA ukouslo příliš velké sousto a nestíhalo ho pořádně zapít a přežvýkat. Hráči často kritizují velikosti map. Vytýkají hře větší soustředění na užší prostory, menší mapy a interiéry. Tady budu ale na straně EA. Styl jakým se Battlefield 6 hraje, jak přistupuje k poškození, TTK, mechanikám ve hře apod. přímo koresponduje s velikostí map. Prakticky tu platí pravý opak na který jsme u série Battlefield zvyklý. Menší, kompaktnější a smrštěnější režimy a mapy tu fungují o poznání lépe. Escalation, Domination a Teamdeathmatch jsou za mě 3 režimy, které dodnes nepotřebují rework, doladění ani nic podobného. V Battlefieldu 6 fungují naprosto perfektně a s nabídkou aktuálních map, pro tyto zmíněné režimy, nemám nejmenší problém. 
Oproti tomu takový Conquest je dost rozporuplný. Battlefieldu 6 totiž láme vaz zmíněný přechod na rychlejší styl hraní. V Conquestu je až neskonalý zmatek, TTK je zkrátka pro tento režim příliš nízký. Když už jsem se tu otřel o téma Map, tak tady určitě zmíním mírnou kritiku k vizuálu a výběru. Až na pár vyjímek tu máme celkem nešťastný design map. Chybí u nich balanc, dynamika...Kupříkladu vytoužená mapa Operation Firestorm. Prakticky nejoblíbenější mapa v Battlefieldu 3. Tady? Bezesporu jedna z horších. Nefunguje správně. To co bylo skvělé v pomalejším Battlefieldu 3, se tady v případě Operation Firestormu setkává s naprostým neúspěchem. Nebál bych se tvrdit, že díky tomu jakým stylem se hraje BF6 apod. je aktuálně Operation Firestorm tou nejhorší mapou pro Battlefield 6. Nesmím ani opomenout grafické zpracování. Rozumím tomu, že na mapách s velkou destrukcí a porcí efektů a výbuchů je potřeba počítat s určitým grafickým kompromisem, ale i tady se opět dostáváme k naprosté nekonzistenci. Některé mapy vypadají graficky velmi slušně, jiné oproti tomu jako early 2010...2015? Schválně si zkuste porovnat grafický styl a detaily v Battlefieldu 5. Nechci tvrdit, že Battlefield 6 je ošklivou hrou, to ani zdaleka. Jen mi graficky přijde ''nezačištěný'' a chvílemi...vyblitý? To by bylo asi to slovo. 

Další téma je obsah. 
Battlefield 6 a celé EA již daleko před samotným vydáním slibovalo naprostou revoluci, návrat ke kořenům. Revoluce se nekoná, to by možná ani nikdo nechtěl...návrat ke kořenům? To už vůbec né. Ale proboha. Jak může studio, které má za sebou Battlefield 3 a 4, takhle prachsprostě promarnit svůj potenciál. S liveservicem modelem problém nemám, naopak ho vítám, ale tady je téměř po roce zkrátka zřejmé, že studio mělo velké oči ale skutek utekl. Minimum nových map, ty nové mapy jsou opravdu strašné, Battlepass je sice hezká věc, ale musí umět motivovat, to je základní premisou přece. Když porovnám Battlepassy a content i s velmi špatným Battlefieldem 2042, tak i ten vítězí na plné čáře. Proč zkrátka studio nevezme veškeré mapy z Battlefieldu 3, neprožene je grafickým overhaulem a nekrmí nás? To je přece minimum práce. :D Vrchol ignoranství je prosinec 2025. 90% hráčů doma, zvýšená aktivita a oni? Vzali si dovolenou. Vyprdli jeden vánoční event a tím to pro ně končilo. Nakonec přišel i odklad plánované sezony, protože se nestíhalo. A když pak vyšla nová sezóna, tak se nejeden hráč ptal ''Co to studio vlastně dělá''. 

Lehce se otřu o režim RedSec. To je prakticky free to play varianta jakéhokoliv Battleroyalu, který už znáte.
Překvapivě ze začátku zábavný režim nabízí i některé originální mechaniky, které opepří hratelnost. Ale zase a opět se dostáváme k tomu stejnému. Po pár hodinách se jedná o úmorně nudnou záležitost. Zapomeňte na to, že by se Redsec mohl byť jen rovnat králům jako je Fortnite či Warzone. Né nadarmo jsou tyto hry úspěšné a na vrcholu. Redsec selhává v designu mapy, grafickém downgradu, nevybalancovanosti jako v multiplayeru a nedostatku contentu. Nebudu ani zmiňovat to, že téměř po roce stále nemáme solo režim. To měla být samozřejmost už při vydání.

Na závěr kritického yapování musím zmínit netcode a samotný hitreg. Při vydání to byl naprosto největší problém, aktuálně je situace určitě lepší ale stále je co zlepšovat.

Pokud bych měl vytáhnout jeden a zcela zásadní problém Battlefieldu 6, pak to bude určitě nenaplněný potenciál a nedostatek contentu. 

Můžete tvrdit, že jsem blázen, že mám ve hře 200 hodin (i to je ale málo, vážení) a čekám, že mě hra bude držet 500 hodin in. Jenže tady se bavíme o hře, která se od samotného začátku tváří jako liveservice titul, který budete hrát víceméně celý rok. To se ale nekoná a studio moc dobře ví, že to pos*alo. Klesající čísla odpovídají tomu, co se aktuálně děje. Pozitivním na samotný závěr může být ale to, že pár dní zpět naslibovalo EA roadmapu plnou zajímavých novinek. Dočkáme se solo režimu pro Redsec, vypadá to na návrat více jak jedné mapy z původních BF3 a BF4 apod. Naděje sice umírá poslední, ale věřit naplnění dalších ambicioźních gest na sociálních sítích...to je těžké po rozpačitém startu hry.

Závěrem dodám jen takové ujasnění. 

Nechápejte mě špatně, Battlefield 6 je stále jedním z nejlepších Battlefieldů ever. Je setsakra zábavný a umí pohltit na desítky hodin...Jen si s sebou stále bohužel nese tu hořkou pachuť toho, že tohle i tamto by mohlo být lepší a proč tu není tohle apod. Stále je to pro mě nejvíc promarněný potenciál v sérii Battlefield. Nezbývá než doufat v nápravu. 

Pro casuála je to ale naprostý must have titul. Ty 4 hodiny týdně si užije, dostane výbuchy, atmosféru apod.

Tryhardi a MP veteráni, buďte obezřetní do čeho plánujete vložit stovky hodin a neočekávejte propracovaný liveservice jako u konkurentů.

[b]O Battlefield que a gente esperava ([i]e merecia[/i])[/b]

Finalmente a alma da franquia está de volta!

Depois de algumas idas e vindas da DICE nos últimos anos, esse BF chega com aquele "[i]feeling[/i]" que eu não sentia desde a época de ouro do BF3 e do BF4. É difícil explicar, mas quem viveu o auge desses jogos sabe do que estou falando: é o peso do boneco, o impacto do [i]gunplay[/i] e aquela imersão sonora que faz você realmente se sentir no meio de um caos controlado.

[b]O que brilha:[/b]
Jogabilidade Raiz: A movimentação está muito mais responsiva e o combate entre infantaria e veículos parece ter achado o ponto de equilíbrio perfeito de novo. Não parece algo "flutuante"; cada tiro e cada explosão têm peso.

Imersão: O design de som continua sendo o melhor da indústria. Jogar isso aqui com um bom fone é uma experiência de guerra total. O clima nos mapas remete diretamente aos mapas urbanos clássicos que a gente tanto ama.

Destruição: Voltaram a focar no que importa. Ver o cenário mudando conforme a partida avança não é só estético, é estratégico, exatamente como nos velhos tempos... levolution ta muito maneiro!! (pode melhorar) mas ta muito maneiro!

Pés no chão (Pontos a melhorar):
Claro, nem tudo é perfeito. Como qualquer lançamento dessa magnitude hoje em dia, o jogo ainda tem suas arestas para aparar. Encontrei alguns bugs de colisão e o netcode precisa de um ajuste fino em servidores mais cheios.

Porém, a grande diferença aqui é a postura dos desenvolvedores. Dá para notar que a comunidade está sendo ouvida. Já saíram atualizações focadas justamente no que a galera pediu no beta e nos primeiros dias. Nenhum jogo hoje sai 100% polido, mas o que importa é o comprometimento em deixar o jogo redondo, e isso eu estou vendo acontecer.

Veredito:
Se você é órfão do BF3/BF4 e estava desanimado com os rumos da franquia, pode dar uma chance. O jogo tem alma, tem o DNA de Battlefield e, com o suporte que está recebendo, tem tudo para ser o melhor dos últimos dez anos.
